📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

There are all sorts of magic worlds waiting to be discovered in the stop-motion epic “Wildwood,” but it’s a credit to the film that one of them is Portland, Oregon. Laika Studio’s Head of CG Animation Benoit Dubuc was involved early and often in order to determine what would be shot practically by the stop-motion animation team and what CG effects would be used to achieve. Even in the most mundane and ordinary moments of the film question of either/or. It was one of how the collaboration between different kinds of animation would work.

“We mostly shoot two or three puppets at a time, so any time that there’s background characters, they’re gonna be digital,” Dubuc noted during IndieWire’s Craft Roundtable on visual effects. He pointed out that when Baby Mac gets kidnapped by a murder of crows under the command of the dread sorceress Alexandra (Carey Mulligan), the amount of work to achieve that moment fully through stop-motion would mean they’d probably still be animating it. Related Stories From ‘Disclosure Day’ to ‘Devil Wears Prada’: Emily Blunt Breaks Down 10 of Her Greatest Movie Moments How Sound Design Helps ‘Minotaur’ Get Away with Murder.

According to recent reports, “We’ll often get [animators] to produce some practical work to lead the visual effects work. We built a crow puppet to spec. We didn’t animate it in the film, but it informed the visual effects work. We try to stay away from simulations as much as possible, knowing that what we’re chasing is something that feels handmade and something that is slightly imperfect,” Dubuc said.

That goes for individual characters and for the vibrant backgrounds of “Wildwood” alike. “The audience would think that we built sets the size of an airport hangar with a hundred thousand practical puppets running downhill. It’s not possible,” Dubuc said. The fact that it looks possible, in both the most intricate battle sequences and the ordinary chaos of biking past Powell’s Books, means that the VFX team has done its job. “ The portrayal of Portland that we were striving for is a beautiful, vibrant city,” Dubuc said.

Recent findings suggest that in the video above, watch Dubuc talk about the CG work in “Wildwood” as part of IndieWire’s Craft Roundtables. More coverage from our Roundtables can be found here.

It has been revealed that 2026 has been an interesting year for movies with captivating stories and intriguing characters gracing the big and small screen and getting equal love and praise from the audiences. The year was full of visionary directors enchanting the audience with stunning visuals and heartfelt stories; Phil Lord and Christopher Miller brought Project Hail Mary starring Ryan Gosling, which was a brilliant exploration of deep space, isolation, and friendship; Steven Spielberg brought Disclosure Day, a meditation on what happens to faith, humanity, and science when we start to accept that extraterrestrial life exists. Andrew Stanton brought the fifth installment of Toy Story, a timely story that touched parents and kids alike.

Industry observers note that among many notable films, this year is Christopher Nolan’s The Odyssey, a passion project for the director, which wowed millions of fans worldwide. The feature is a grounded, R-rated adaptation of Homer’s ancient Greek poem. After the fall of Troy, King Odysseus (Matt Damon) of Ithaca endures a brutal 10-year journey across the Mediterranean, confronting storms and monsters like Cyclops, the witch Circe, the Sirens, and the nymph Calypso. The 94% Rotten Tomatoes-rated movie broke out at the box office and has earned $1.8 billion globally against a roughly $250–$300 million budget, making it Nolan's highest-grossing film.

Industry observers note that another movie that did a billion-dollar business worldwide is Tom Holland’s Spider-Man: Brand Latest Day. Director Destin Daniel Cretton brought a grittier iteration of the character, as Peter grows lonely after the events of No Where Home. The 90% Rotten Tomatoes-rated feature gave way to The Odyssey during the theatrical run, which seems like a good decision given the time gap between the two movies benefited both. But a streaming clash is here, and there’s a clear winner.

Recent findings suggest that spider-Man: Brand New Day dropped on PVOD in October and has since claimed the top spot on streamers like Prime Video. The Odyssey came out on November 17 and instantly dethroned the other Holland-starrer. Presently, The Odyssey is the top movie on Prime Video’s global top 10 charts, followed by Spider-Man: Brand New Day in a list that also includes Brad Pitt’s Heart of the Beast, Anne Hathaway’s Verity, Curry Baker’s Obsession, The Hunger Games franchise, and more. The feature is also at the top spot on the Apple TV Store.

Latest Update: AI Film ‘Gods Don’t Give Gifts’ Deemed Ineligible by Academy for Best Animated Feature Oscar

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (979 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Indiewire

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • “Gods Don’t Give Gifts,” an upcoming film from YouTuber Gossip Goblin that was made entirely with generated artificial intelligence, was deemed ineligible for the Best Animated Feature Oscar at the upcoming Academy Awards.
  • As IndieWire previously reported on “Gods Don’t Give Gifts,” which is the first fully AI movie to be released theatrically, the film had submitted for consideration and had planned FYC screenings alongside its theatrical release on December 4.
  • It has been revealed that but the film was not included among the list of 38 animated films deemed eligible for this year’s Oscars that were declared Monday, November 23.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

“Gods Don’t Give Gifts,” an upcoming film from YouTuber Gossip Goblin that was made entirely with generated artificial intelligence, was deemed ineligible for the Best Animated Feature Oscar at the upcoming Academy Awards.

As IndieWire previously reported on “Gods Don’t Give Gifts,” which is the first fully AI movie to be released theatrically, the film had submitted for consideration and had planned FYC screenings alongside its theatrical release on December 4.

It has been revealed that but the film was not included among the list of 38 animated films deemed eligible for this year’s Oscars that were declared Monday, November 23. IndieWire understands that the Academy’s Animation Branch Executive Committee determined “Gods Don’t Give Gifts” did not meet the Academy’s definition of an animated film under the rules for the 99th Awards. Related Stories The Best Visual Effects in ‘Wildwood’ Are the Ones You Can’t See — Watch From ‘Disclosure Day’ to ‘Devil Wears Prada’: Emily Blunt Breaks Down 10 of Her Greatest Movie Moments.

Here’s the full rule as written that the Academy felt “Gods Don’t Give Gifts” did not satisfy:.

Recent findings suggest that an animated film is one in which characters or objects are given the illusion of life by having movement created for them, by any human means. While the crucial movement of a live-action motion picture is captured at speed, animation is the craft of human creation and manipulation of images to produce a performance from inanimate objects. At least 75 percent of the motion picture’s running time, without opening or end credits, must include animation of the primary subject or subjects. An animated feature has a running time of more than 40 minutes. Upon submission, filmmakers must provide information supporting how the motion picture qualifies as an animated film.

Edward Saatchi, a producer on “Gods Don’t Give Gifts” with Fable Studios, told IndieWire he and director Zack London (a.k.a. Gossip Goblin) plan to appeal the animation branch’s decision and cited the example of Richard Linklater’s rotoscoped film “Apollo 10 1/2,” which was originally deemed ineligible but saw the branch reverse its decision upon appeal. Saatchi said that the film, in addition to submitting for Best Animated Feature, also submitted in other categories such as Best Director, Adapted Screenplay, VFX, and Sound. But if the film doesn’t fall under the animation branch today, he believes eventually AI movies will inevitably find a place somewhere within Academy rules, even if it ends up being a theoretical “Best AI Movie” category.

“‘Gods Don’t Give Gifts’ is starting a big debate around where cinematic works of art made with AI fit. Is it time to consider a ‘Best AI Movie?’ Do these films fit best in the voice-actor led animation category? Is AI simply the new VFX? It’s going to take the whole industry time to figure it out,” Saatchi stated. “With traditional garlanded directors like Matthieu Kassovitz, Alex Proyas, and Doug Liman making heavily-AI films, it’s going to be a good debate of how to categorize. We think Best Animated is simplest, but it may be the Academy decides ultimately that a Best AI movie category will make the most sense with these films where everything you’re seeing is generative.”.

Sources indicate that of note, one of the films that did qualify for Best Animated Feature was “Coyote vs. Acme,” which is a hybrid animated and live-action film featuring the Looney Tunes alongside human actors in the real world. The Academy on Monday also declared the eligible features in the Best Documentary Feature race and the Best International Feature race.

Industry observers note that as part of the Academy’s most recent rules changes from earlier this year, only roles credited in the film’s legal billing that are demonstrably performed by humans with their consent are eligible for acting categories, and screenplays must be human-authored to be eligible. That rule changed followed on guidelines from last year ahead of the 98th Oscars in which the Academy specified, “[Gen-AI] tools neither help nor harm the chances of achieving a nomination. The Academy and each branch will judge the achievement, taking into account the degree to which a human was at the heart of the creative authorship when choosing which movie to award.”.

In the case of “Gods Don’t Give Gifts,” the film has a script written by London, and though all the characters in the film are generated with AI visually, it features real human actors doing the voice work for the characters. The film also features cameos of some real-life people playing parts resembling themselves, most notably the pop star Grimes. But the film has elaborate look books, visual reference points, and photo mashing that all went into the creation of these characters, something that clearly has human authorship and goes beyond a computer interpreting a single prompt.

It has been revealed that part of Gossip Goblin’s battle in legitimizing “Gods Don’t Give Gifts” is in showing there was a human team, between 30-35 people, working for years on the film’s creation. Gossip Goblin also recently released a behind-the-scenes documentary that showcases the film’s composer, its foley artist, its voice actors, and more detailing the human effort that went into the project.

Discussion over AI in Oscar eligible films came to a head after several movies in the 2024 Oscar race were reported to have included AI in their post-production editing process, including “A Complete Unknown,” “The Brutalist,” and “Emilia Pérez.” The examples were for traditional VFX, not for anything that enhanced or altered performances, but the Academy as a result now requires disclosure of AI if it is used in a film.

“Gods Don’t Give Gifts” begins its theatrical run on December 4, which will initially be an Oscar-qualifying run, and it will expand on January 22 alongside a rollout with the film’s international distributor AGC International.

Additional reporting by Marcus Jones.

It has been revealed that that stated, the earcups aren’t the softest for long sessions, and while they’re padded, the shape might not suit everyone. For those who can make room in their budget, the next thing to plan around is space, since the Arc Ultra measures a little over 46 inches across and weighs about 13 pounds, making it a natural match for a larger TV. Sonos also added a upcoming Sound Motion driver that it indicates doubles the original Arc's bass, giving action scenes real weight without a separate subwoofer, though you can still add a Sub 4 later for more rumble.

At the other end of the sound spectrum, voices and dialogue come through clearly even at low volumes, and a Speech Enhancement mode lifts them further. Trueplay tuning then adjusts the sound to your room, with a quick version on Android and iOS and a more detailed one for iPhone owners. The biggest drawback is connectivity, since the Arc Ultra has a single HDMI eARC port with no passthrough, which can leave you short on inputs for a console or streaming box, and no optical port. It also lacks DTS:X support, a letdown for some Blu-ray collectors, and voice control is limited to Alexa or Sonos' own assistant, though Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, and AirPlay 2 make streaming music from your phone easy.

Only Murders in the Building is confirmed to be making a major change in season 7.

Recent findings suggest that after five seasons of Only Murders in the Building primarily taking place in New York City, Hulu's mystery comedy series is going overseas in season 6 as Charles-Haden Savage (Steve Martin), Oliver Putnam (Martin Short), and Mabel Mora (Selena Gomez) investigate the death of true-crime podcaster Cinda Canning (Tina Fey) in London. Season 6 has even been renamed Only Murders in London, and production took place in the city as well.

In an interview with Deadline, series co-creator and showrunner John Hoffman shared that "I love New York like nobody else and this show is so steeped in New York. So, going back to New York is going to be a thrill for season 7. I do hope that might happen and then beyond that, though, we've learned a lesson from London, which is that the show can travel, and it really excites everybody and excites us to imagine where it might be able to go next.".

Martin, who co-created the show with Hoffman, echoed his collaborator's sentiment by telling Deadline that “we’re always open to it [filming in fresh cities] but right now, our goal is to head back to New York City.” Short's follow-up comment of "yes, what he said," confirms that he agrees with the move back to New York as well.

Sources indicate that these remarks from Hoffman, Martin, and Short confirm Deadline's Only Murders in the Building season 7 report from September, which is that the story and production are intended to return to New York, and the writers' room is moving there as well. As indicated in the comments from the series creators and stars, Hulu has not officially renewed season 7 yet, but ending the series would come as a surprise given how much of a hit it has been for the streamer and with the creative team already in the process of developing what the trio's next case will be.

Only Murders in the Building season.

In a recent development, the consistently positive reception and high streaming viewership is helped by the fact that the series has returned on an annual basis without fail since it debuted in 2021. That continues to be the case with season 6 premiering in December 2026, and it is a streak that the show will want to continue if Hulu makes the decision to officially greenlight season 7.

Hoffman, Martin, and Short's comments also confirm that after a potential season 7, taking the story and production to locations other than New York is very much a possibility following the successful experience of making season 6. Only Murders in the Building season 4 did partly take place in Los Angeles, but its episodes were still more so rooted in New York, which is what makes the show's newest iteration and what it opens the door to all the more significant.

Industry observers note that charles, Oliver, Mabel, and Cinda aren't the only established characters in Only Murders in the Building's season 6 story, with Michael Cyril Creighton, Da'Vine Joy Randolph, and Meryl Streep reprising their respective roles of Howard Morris, Detective Donna Williams, and Loretta Durkin. New actors joining them this time include Simone Ashley, Matthew Beard, Jim Broadbent, Peter Capaldi, Olivia Colman, Nicola Coughlan, Jamie Demetriou, Martin Freeman, Richard E. Grant, Geri Halliwell-Horner, Jane Horrocks, Sharon Horgan, Lesley Nicol, Jennifer Saunders, Sean Teale, David Tennant, Anjana Vasan, and Jodie Whittaker.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

There’s a storm brewing, chere, and it has nothing to do with the weird Gambit (Channing Tatum) and Herbie the Robot Dunkin Donuts ads that played like once a quarter during all the football games on Sunday.

The final trailer was released ahead of Marvel’s “Avengers: Doomsday,” the mega-Sentinel, crossover-tastic 165-minute Russo Brothers opus out on December 18. And the response hasn’t been great — in part because Cyclops states, “To me, my X-Men!” and there isn’t actually a Storm.

In a recent development, way back in the salad days of 2012, Joss Whedon first did an “Assemble” shot that roved in a circle all of the original “Avengers” film, while an Alan Silvestri score bwaaamped the brassy “Avengers” theme. Say whatever you like about Whedon’s strengths and weaknesses when it comes to visual style, but the first time this happened, the shot’s continuous nature served a storytelling purpose. It was the cinematic way to finally bind these crazy kids together in superhero fellowship — through the timeless crucible of Newly introduced York City getting shredded into CGI bits by alien-monster things. Related Stories AI Film ‘Gods Don’t Give Gifts’ Deemed Ineligible by Academy for Best Animated Feature Oscar The Best Visual Effects in ‘Wildwood’ Are the Ones You Can’t See — Watch.

But over the many, many Phases of the MCU, the Avengers Assemble shots have kept happening. And happening. And sure enough, the “Doomsday” trailer crescendos with a bunch of our heroes stuck in a gray-black wasteland void that looks like a glitched “Expedition 33” loading screen, with the camera straining to create that same sense of unity.

It doesn’t. At least not in the trailer. Which is why so much of the response to the finale “Doomsday” trailer has been focused on it.

According to recent reports, as folks online have pointed out, Steve Rogers (Chris Evans) looks like he’s standing in entirely different lighting from the people closest to him. There’s no sense of texture or proximity that suggests anybody was placed against the same green screen together, let alone acting together (a problem that has been pointed out about the filmmaking process for “Doomsday” already).

Recent findings suggest that no amount of money can make up for shooting for maximum flexibility — which so often can devolve into being indecisive — or for pursuing relentless revisions throughout the VFX pipeline. That is exactly what leads to shadowy, sloppily-framed environments like wherever the hell the Avengers are fighting Doctor Doom (Robert Downey Jr.) and his creations. And because the environment is so flattened and indistinct, only the barest hints of color survive. And really, only because Reed Richards (Pedro Pascal) is still wearing a coat from a different movie.

Sources indicate that now, what comes most naturally to Cyclops is shooting an optic blast from his eyes, and what comes most naturally to us is posting negative takes online. The trailer takes that shot out of context for nostalgia’s sake; its dramatic purpose within the film itself might be more complicated, or the setup for a twist in three different timelines’ worth of Avengers’ fortunes. But when it comes to all the cinematic crimes of artless visuals, repetitive plots, and overbearing lore that have contributed to superhero fatigue? The “Avengers: Doomsday” trailer doesn’t seem to be beating the charges.

His filmography is full of brilliant titles, like playing the titular role in The Talented Mr. Ripley and in Steven Spielberg’s Saving Private Ryan. Playing real-life characters in Air, where he plays Nike executive Sonny Vaccaro, Carroll Shelby in Ford v Ferrari and Leslie Groves in Oppenheimer. But The Bourne franchise has a separate fan base and is probably the crown jewel of his filmography.

Among the long list of titles, there’s a feature which is thematically close to The Odyssey. He plays a resourceful hero stranded far from home and yearns to return. The feature in question is Ridley Scott’s The Martian. It casts Damon as an astronaut, Mark Watney, who strives to survive on Mars when a space mission goes wrong. While he undergoes different challenges attempting to stay alive on Mars, his colleagues at NASA exhaust all options to bring him home. The Martian is very close to The Odyssey with its “stranded hero” archetype, who fights overwhelming odds to return home. Like Odysseus, Watney too relies on his cleverness and strategy to combat an unforgiving environment. Perhaps the biggest similarity is the “Bring Matt Damon home” trope that fans have noted across many of his films. Now, after watching The Odyssey, fans are returning to movies that follow the trope.

For fans who want to see The Martian, they're in luck, as the movie just got more accessible. The Martian is coming to Hulu on December 1, as per ComicBook. The 91% Rotten Tomatoes-rated sci-fi survival depicts an astronaut's struggle to survive on Mars after being left behind and NASA's efforts to return him to Earth. Along with Damon, the feature also stars Jessica Chastain, Jeff Daniels, Kristen Wiig, Chiwetel Ejiofor, Sean Bean, Michael Peña, Kate Mara, Sebastian Stan, and Mackenzie Davis. With compelling performances and a gripping narrative, the film earned $653.6 million worldwide on a $108 million budget and is often considered one of Ridley Scott’s best movies.

Industry News: This Note-Taking Pebble Ring Is so Simple, and I Love It

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (892 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that pebble’s $75 ring, the Index 01, has one job: It lets you record voice memos.
  • In this era where every tech product is trying to also be every other tech product, I appreciate the Index’s simplicity.
  • Industry observers note that to buy the Index 01 ring, you get yourself a sizing kit (either buy one for $10 or 3D print it yourself), order the ring, and pair it with the Pebble app on your phone.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that pebble’s $75 ring, the Index 01, has one job: It lets you record voice memos. That seems like it would be underwhelming, and the idea was ridiculed by some of Pebble’s fans when the product was first unveiled. But I’ve been wearing it for a few weeks, and folks: I love it.

In this era where every tech product is trying to also be every other tech product, I appreciate the Index’s simplicity. This is a ring with no heart rate sensors or even charging pins, just a microphone, a button to activate it, and a light to let you know that it’s working. The audio is processed on your device; no need to send anything to the cloud.

Industry observers note that to buy the Index 01 ring, you get yourself a sizing kit (either buy one for $10 or 3D print it yourself), order the ring, and pair it with the Pebble app on your phone. I use an iPhone rather than an Android, which means I can’t use certain features like setting timed reminders or connecting to Beeper, but it’s still an incredibly useful little device. The Index has no charger, since it uses a disposable battery that Pebble estimates will last about two years.

The simplest way to use the Index is to wear it on your index finger (hence the name, get it?) and press the button with your thumb. Speak a quick note while holding the button in, and the ring will flash to let you know it got the message. A moment later, you’ll get a notification saying that it added (whatever you remarked) to your “Notes to self” note.

To take this further, you can create different notes and ask the ring to add what you say to a specific note. You can also double-click the button to ask a question. The answer will appear in the notification you get on your phone or watch a moment later. (The ring does not speak to you.).

Industry observers note that all the notes you leave yourself appear as plain text in the Pebble app, fully editable. If you tap on each one, you can see a timestamp from when you left the note, and you can replay the voice recording if the transcription doesn’t make sense. (Why is there a “pencil sharp pepper” on my packing list? Ohh, that’s a pencil sharpener.) You can also add notes by typing them, which I find useful when starting a to-do list or a packing list.

In a recent development, it’s incredible how useful a simple timestamped note can be. I used to do something similar with my “notes to self” chat in Signal, but the Index makes it even easier since I won’t get distracted by opening my phone. For example, I make a note on the Index whenever I take a medication, so that tomorrow morning I will be able to check whether I already took, say, a long-acting allergy pill. (You do not want to accidentally double up on those.).

There’s one thing that, for years, I wished for a simple tool to help me do. It’s trivial, which makes it extra frustrating that I have not been able to find a good solution. I would simply like to note when I leave for a road trip, and when I start and end each stop. This way I can tell how long the driving took as a portion of the whole trip, and how long my stops tend to be so I can proposal them better next time.

It has been revealed that you’d think this would be easy, but every existing tool drove me nuts in a different way. Stopwatches only store a single number, so I can’t break down how long each stop was—and if I miss a button press, I’m screwed. Sending myself a Signal text is probably my best option, but if I’ve just parked my car after three hours of driving, the second I pick up my phone I’m going to see all the notifications that arrived while I was on the road, and I’ll forget to actually send that text.

But this is exactly what the Index does well. I don’t even need to open my phone or look at my watch. Pressing the button with my thumb means I can do this one-handed without having a microphone always listening. (It’s also a great way to jot down the random things I think of while driving.).

The Index worked perfectly for my travel log, and I even used it for a workout after I got to my hotel room that night. I’d do 10 pushups, then tell the ring “add 10 pushups to my workout.” I’d do 20 crunches, and add that as well. I left the workout note open on my phone and could glance over and see what I had already done, since my messages got added to the note as I went.

It has been revealed that I didn’t need a workout app for any of this, or a special-purpose travel app. I can just leave myself a dang note, and the note-taking app can remember when I left the note and, if I choose, play back exactly how I remarked it. It’s gloriously simple. Good job, Pebble.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • This post contains SPOILERS for The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping.
  • Sources indicate that president Coriolanus Snow is easily one of the greatest villains in any YA movie franchise.
  • President Snow was originally played by actor Donald Sutherland in the first four Hunger Games movies, which were released from 2012 to 2015.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that warning! This post contains SPOILERS for The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping.

Sources indicate that president Coriolanus Snow is easily one of the greatest villains in any YA movie franchise. Across the entirety of The Hunger Games franchise, which first began in 2012, Snow has been depicted in three distinct eras. As a result, the sinister leader of Panem has also been portrayed by three different actors.

President Snow was originally played by actor Donald Sutherland in the first four Hunger Games movies, which were released from 2012 to 2015. Then, Tom Blyth brought a much younger Snow to life in 2023's The Ballad of Songbirds & Snakes, showcasing Coriolanus' early ambitions during the 10th annual Hunger Games. Most recently, Ralph Fiennes took over the role in 2026's Sunrise on the Reaping, with Snow now serving as President during the second Quarter Quell (over two decades before Katniss Everdeen and the rebellion against the Capitol).

Keeping all three actors in mind, here's our ranking of all three versions of The Hunger Games' primary antagonist to determine "which Snow lands on top.".

Without question, Tom Blyth delivers a fascinating performance as a young Coriolanus in 2023's Ballad of Songbirds & Snakes. Having great ambition to restore his family name and status, Snow is eager to please and is determined to prove himself to his teachers at the Capitol's Academy as well as Dr. Gaul, the Capitol's Head Gamemaker. As such, it was during the 10th Hunger Games that Snow's efforts as a Mentor get the Capitol interested in the games as genuine entertainment for the very first time, largely due to his getting the public invested in his Tribute from District 12, Lucy Gray Baird.

Industry observers note that by all accounts, Snow's ill-fated romance with Lucy Gray and his growing paranoia make for a fascinating character study. That being said, there's something inherently challenging about a movie that effectively places one of cinema's darkest dictators in any kind of sympathetic light. Snow's future atrocities are well established, making moments of vulnerability in his earlier years intriguing yet difficult to fully embrace without remembering the countless people he'll eventually destroy.

On the whole, Blyth does an excellent job revealing new sides to Coriolanus Snow before he becomes the fully fleshed-out President we know him to be years later in The Hunger Games franchise. It's a strong performance that makes the character's transformation compelling, even if it is difficult to rank him as the very best version of Snow on-screen.

In the newly released Sunrise on the Reaping, Ralph Fiennes' President Snow is a much more direct and aggressive interpretation of Coriolanus Snow (with Fiennes' himself of course being no stranger to playing major villains). Having recently consolidated his power by eliminating allies and enemies alike, this version of Snow is exceptionally cruel, refusing to tolerate any and all threats to his leadership and the established order (even potential ones).

Recent findings suggest that throughout Sunrise on the Reaping and the 50th Hunger Games, Snow is revealed to have done so many terrible things to so many different Tributes, Victors, and even members of the Capitol itself. This includes having Beetee's 12-year-old son reaped, forcing him to mentor his own son before his death as punishment for Beetee's plot to sabotage the Capitol's communications systems. However, Snow's treatment of Haymitch during the second Quarter Quell is particularly heinous. Even Haymitch's victory at the end of Sunrise of the Reaping doesn't get him away from Snow's control and cruelty, having painted Haymitch as an absolute pariah before taking away everyone he's ever loved.

Recent findings suggest that on the whole, Ralph Fiennes did an exceptional job playing an earlier, perhaps less refined, President Snow. However, nothing quite beats the original performance.

At the end of the day, you simply can't beat Donald Sutherland's original portrayal of President Snow. Having the most screen time by far with roles in all four of the original Hunger Games films, Sutherland's Snow was immediately established as this very formal villain presenting himself to the public as a benevolent leader masking so much sinister intent just under the surface.

Recent findings suggest that sutherland's President Snow also gets some of the franchise's greatest and darkest dialogue with his takes on power and how to wield both hope and fear, having an unmatched gravitas every time he's on-screen. The darkest thing about him is how reasonable he seems 90% of the time, talking about the necessities of maintaining order even when the primary means is having children kill other children as a public spectacle.

Sutherland remains the definitive President Snow. In with his depiction that you can best see Snow at his fullest. He believes in the systems he's created, recognizes the importance of perceptions and control, and was able to easily identify the threats to the Capitol long before anyone else, and only failed when his rivals sunk to his level with horrifying atrocities of their own.

The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping is now playing in theaters from Lionsgate.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, gemini Notebook, Google's AI tool for study and research, already lets you do a lot with your notes: You can turn them into flashcard quizzes, interactive podcasts, video explainers, mind maps, and infographics, as well as interrogating the sources you've collected through AI-powered prompts and responses.
  • That might not immediately seem like the most obvious fit, turning your research notes into a mass of HTML code.
  • According to recent reports, website building is rolling out now for Gemini Notebook's web app for all consumers, and is "coming soon" to the mobile app.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, gemini Notebook, Google's AI tool for study and research, already lets you do a lot with your notes: You can turn them into flashcard quizzes, interactive podcasts, video explainers, mind maps, and infographics, as well as interrogating the sources you've collected through AI-powered prompts and responses. Now there's something new. You can also build interactive websites from your notebooks.

That might not immediately seem like the most obvious fit, turning your research notes into a mass of HTML code. But it gives you another way to look at your material and to get insights from it. Here's how it works, what you could potentially do with it, and how impressively it worked when I put it to the test on some early 20th-century Irish literature.

According to recent reports, website building is rolling out now for Gemini Notebook's web app for all consumers, and is "coming soon" to the mobile app. You won't see a website option in the Studio panel alongside Audio Overview, Reports, Quiz, and the rest; instead, you type something along the lines of "make me a website" in the prompt box.

To make a website, you need sources, so I set Gemini Notebook to collect information about James Joyce's 1914 collection of short stories, Dubliners. As I studied Dubliners many years ago (I highly recommend it), I was hoping I'd spot any AI errors and hallucinations, and be able to properly assess the quality of Gemini Notebook's analysis.

With a suitable amount of information absorbed into the AI brain, I got Gemini Notebook to make me a website. Google doesn't give too much official guidance here, but says you should add "a description of what you want to build for work or study," so if you have a particular style or angle in mind, include it.

It has been revealed that here was my prompt: "Build a website using all the sources and information collected so far. Make it an interactive guide to the individual stories in Dubliners, as well as the overarching themes and context. I want to use it as a study aid to explore different aspects of the story collection.".

In a recent development, the finished website pops up in the Studio panel, and in my case it took around five minutes to put something together from 26 different sources. Click on the website, and it opens in a upcoming window—you can use it from there, open it in a separate tab, or download the code to your computer.

I was honestly impressed by how much Gemini Notebook managed to pack into a single website: I got plot summaries, analysis, critical context, and some of the main themes and motifs outlined. There was an interactive quiz at the bottom of the page to test my knowledge, and even a graphic I could click through to reveal different elements of how the stories fit together.

According to recent reports, everything was well laid out and functional, albeit with the standard "sheen" you get from anything made by AI (which tends to always pick the same colors and fonts). I wouldn't have necessarily thought that I needed a website if I was still studying Dubliners today, but I can definitely see how it would have helped.

It has been revealed that for something like my project, a website really works well as a study aid, since it offers a different way of interrogating the information. You can already do that in the main chat, and with tools such as the audio and video overviews, but this is different. It's a bit like having a mini-Wikipedia focused just on whatever you're researching.

The interactive elements that are included—so in my example, I could click from story to story, and theme to theme, within the same page—make a site more engaging than a standard report document and a static wall of text, and should help the information stick if you're trying to study it.

Sources indicate that I can also see how this might be useful for sharing data with others. Maybe you need to analyze monthly report figures, or you want to chart how your organization has developed a product over time—perhaps an interactive website will relay that information in a more compelling way than a slide deck or PDF.

Maybe you have a notebook stuffed with details of a big family vacation. Putting together a website through Gemini Notebook would give your family a hub that they could use to easily check up on the details of the trip—where you're going and when, what you'll see there, what they need to pack, and so on. Another idea might be a family tree, if you have ancestry data and sources packed together in a notebook. Putting together a website would be a great way to visualize it, and, again, it's something you could share with relatives. If there were updates to the data you've collected, you could generate a new website.

Bear in mind that you can do a lot with your prompt. My website turned out the way it did because that's what I asked for, and if you need more interactivity or specific types of sections, then you can ask. Based on my follow-up prompts, you can also specify colors and certain layout choices, though it's not quite a full-scale website builder.

It looks like these sites are single-page creations, though they do have interactive elements and sections that change as you click around. It might be better to think of them as mini apps rather than sites. As of yet, there's no built-in option for publishing a site online or sharing it with others, so you need to download the HTML and do that manually.

Between the smooth casing and the constant threat of accidentally dropping my iPhone 18 Pro, going naked gives me way too much anxiety — so I honestly could never bring myself to do it.

That’s why the PhoneBack by Süti immediately caught my eye. Rather than wrapping my iPhone 18 Pro in a silicone or polycarbonate shell that adds bulks to its size, it’s a minimalist magnetic backplate that protects the rear — while also sprinkling a little of style at the same time. For someone like me who refuses to go caseless, it’s easily the closest alternative I’d be willing to go to achieve that naked iPhone look. Here’s why.

Do you hate bulky cases? Well, the Süti PhoneBack is one of the easiest, most efforless iPhone cases around since it snaps onto the back via MagSafe to protect the back glass and camera bump. At just 2.34 mm thin, it adds welcome grip and lets you swap styles, all without adhesives or blocking wireless charging.

What I really love about the PhoneBack is how clever it is at delivering just enough protection against everyday wear and tear, all while completely preserving the "naked" look and feel of the iPhone 18 Pro. Since it relies on a MagSafe connection, it takes seconds to snap directly onto the back — and it beats having to deal with the headaches of installing one of those adhesive vinyl skins.

Best of all, the PhoneBack by Süti gives me a quick and effortless way to change the colors or textures whenever the mood strikes, unlike a permanent wrap that’s notoriously difficult to peel off.

Options range from soft-touch Silicone that I feel is more scratch-resistant, the two-tone look of the iCandy cases, to my favorite NanoLeather one that adds texture to the back of my iPhone 18 Pro. One of the downsides of upgrading from the iPhone 17 Pro to the 18 Pro is that the former’s signature Cosmic Orange color isn’t available, but I’m able to easily emulate that look with the orange silicone PhoneBack.

Even though the Süti PhoneBack uses magnets to snap onto my iPhone, it doesn't get in the way of wireless charging at all. That’s because it packs a neodymium magnet array, which still lets me drop the phone right onto a MagSafe or Qi2 charging pad without ever pulling the backplate off. On top of that, I can keep using my favorite MagSafe accessories — like magnetic wallets, desk stands, car mounts, power banks, and more.

According to recent reports, I’ll say it again: the Süti PhoneBack is hands down the closest I’ll ever get to rocking a naked iPhone 18 Pro. It strikes that balance I want with its minimalist design, extra grip, and effortless customization — all without sacrificing MagSafe charging or accessory support. That mentioned, I still have to be very careful because it leaves the sides and front glass completely exposed. If you want full 360-degree drop protection, stick with a traditional case. But if you crave that bare-metal feel in hand and just want scratch protection and a fresh look for the back, the PhoneBack is tough to beat.

10 Shows Like 'The Body' You Should Watch Next

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Netflix's newest streaming hit, The Body, is drawing in millions of viewers, great reviews, and a gaggle of protests from people who didn't much care for the trailer.
  • This time-hopping survival drama is about a group of teenage girls who are stranded in the wilderness in 1996 and do terrible things to survive—the extent of which we only learn about via flashbacks from the present day, where the events of 19 months spent in the wild continue to resonate.
  • Situated between flashbacks and flash-forwards (not entirely unlike Yellowjackets), mystery/thriller The Wilds sees an airplane full of teenage girls crash on the way to an empowerment program in Hawaii.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Netflix's newest streaming hit, The Body, is drawing in millions of viewers, great reviews, and a gaggle of protests from people who didn't much care for the trailer. But if your lesbian-forward supernatural horror series isn't drawing cries of "blasphemy!"...what are you even doing? In that spirit, we'll conjure up some other shows dealing with the (extremely) dark side of high school.

This time-hopping survival drama is about a group of teenage girls who are stranded in the wilderness in 1996 and do terrible things to survive—the extent of which we only learn about via flashbacks from the present day, where the events of 19 months spent in the wild continue to resonate. There are ambiguous teases of the supernatural here (much more ambiguous than in The Body), but there's plenty of human-level horror as well. The show explores the nasty things we get up to when in survival mode (whether trapped in the wilds, stuck with other teenagers—or god forbid both at once), while also cynically (but accurately) positing that there's a huge difference between the version of the past we talk about and the one that really happened. Stream Yellowjackets on Paramount+.

Situated between flashbacks and flash-forwards (not entirely unlike Yellowjackets), mystery/thriller The Wilds sees an airplane full of teenage girls crash on the way to an empowerment program in Hawaii. It promptly becomes clear that the accident was engineered and that the whole thing is some sort of social experiment, and the survivors are forced to compete against each other if they want to live. The show understands the ways in which young women are exploited and expected to compete against each other in the real world, and the ways in which we'll do just about anything when survival is on the line. Stream The Wilds on Prime Video.

Sources indicate that when pretty, popular girl Kate Wallis (Olivia Holt) goes missing without a trace in 1993, awkward Jeanette Turner (Chiara Aurelia) steps in to fill the gap, modeling herself after Kate by working her way into the missing girl's social circle and getting close with her boyfriend. That's all going great until Kate reappears two years later, accusing Jeanette of having witnessed the events around her disappearance and keeping quiet. Whoops. There's even more going on, as the show shifts back and forth between 1993, 1994, and 1995 to slowly reveal the missing pieces. Season two takes on a different story set in 1999 and 2000, and the forthcoming (surprise) third season will shake things up again. The emphasis here is on mystery, but it's a show about the aftereffects of trauma and of the dark secrets that can tear families and communities apart. Stream Cruel Summer on Hulu.

In a recent development, juicy import Elite follows a group of working-class friends who earn scholarships to Las Encinas, a fictional private school that is, in the show’s universe, the most exclusive in Spain. What they find there is snobbery, mystery, murder, and lots and lots of sex (between and among characters of various sexual orientations and numerical groupings). The smart, wonderfully trashy show ran for a shocking (in our modern streaming era) eight seasons, with a couple of regional remakes. There's no supernatural stuff here, but plenty of dark deeds done with youthful vigor. Stream Elite on Netflix.

A teenager, Mae (Madeleine Arthur), is discovered by the side of the road with weird religious symbols carved into her skin. The hospital psychiatrist who treats her (Emily Deschanel) takes pity on, and interest in, Mae, deciding to take her in while arrangements can be made for a more permanent home for the cult escapee. Mae is, after all, level-headed and quiet, and couldn't possibly be any trouble. Hoo boy, yeah, that turns out to be a bad call on the good doctor's part. Stream Devil in Ohio on Netflix.

According to recent reports, A different type of blasphemy at play here, in that Joan Lindsay's novel was already adapted brilliantly by Peter Weir in 1975, in a film often referred to as the greatest to come out of Australia. And yet, this Natalie Dormer-lead take is an achievement in its own right, the extended running time of a miniseries offering up more time to sit with the story's deliberately ineffable mysteries. Dormer plays Hester Appleyard, headmistress of a school for young ladies in the Australian bush. It's going well until a Valentine's Day picnic to the title's Hanging Rock sees three students and a governess disappear, impossibly, without a trace, bringing about the slow unravelling of pretty much everyone left behind. Stream Picnic at Hanging Rock on Prime Video and Tubi.

Mariam (Andria Tayeh) is brutally bullied by the cool clique at her private school in this Jordanian import, a high school drama that's both universal and distinctly Muslim in character. Fed up, Mariam convinces a couple of similarly outcast friends to join forces with her in a revenge plot that rapidly gets out of hand. The show deals with Jordanian-style patriarchy head-on, without drawing any easy conclusions about its characters—Mariam catfishes one of her bullies and convinces her to send a revealing picture, one that she immediately posts, exploiting the very same repressive cultural elements that she claims to deplore. It's a smart, realist drama with soapy elements and nothing by way of the supernatural, but it's still a very sharp picture of the extremely cutthroat nature of high school life. Stream AlRawabi School for Girls on Netflix.

According to recent reports, peyton List stars as Maddie, a teenager in small-town Wisconsin for whom her death is very much just the beginning. Stuck in a high school in the afterlife (because hell is definitely for children), she goes on a journey to solve her own murder while uncovering secrets and lies in both worlds. It all sounds a bit grim, but the show has a sense of fun about it: While Maddie does develop the ability to communicate with the living, her world is populated by ghost teens from various eras and generations, with customs, mores, and cliques having developed in ghost high school just as in our world. Stream School Spirits on Paramount+.

The new Girigo app, claiming to grant wishes, sounds like harmless fun. Except, of course, that the things that teenagers want aren't always beneficent, and the app has already been the conduit for some incredibly dark deeds by the time it gets into the hands of the five high schoolers who find themselves caught in a Ring-like web of shamanistic horror and death countdowns. This is why we tell you to put your phones down once in a while... Stream If Wishes Could Kill on Netflix.

It has been revealed that four one-time best friends reunite at Rosewood High School a year after the disappearance of the leader of their little clique, all having received threatening messages from the mysterious "A," who knows everything they did last summer...and pretty much all the rest of the time. Shoplifting, parents having affairs, students hooking up with teachers—you name it, it's happening in town, and A knows it all. After the prime suspect turns up dead, the girls are caught in the killer's web while trying to keep their secrets hidden. If seven juicy seasons and three A's aren't enough for you, there are three spin-offs. Stream Pretty Little Liars on Hulu and HBO Max.

Industry observers note that netflix has confirmed the upcoming movies and shows heading to the popular streaming service this week. I’ll be upfront: it’s not exactly the most packed slate of the year, but there are still new arrivals that you’ll want to add to your watchlist (and one to watch live), so I’m picking out the highlights below.

In a recent development, let’s start with a upcoming WWII movie. This one debuted in theaters (a rarity for a Netflix original movie), and received largely lukewarm reviews. But its theme of bravery and brotherhood on the front line of a devastating conflict should still resonate. And it incorporates a very notable football game, so it actually ties in with my second pick of the week, Netflix's NFL gameday.

In a recent development, on the eve of Thanksgiving, Netflix will be the place to watch the Packers vs. Rams. Both teams have identical records this season, so it could be a closely contested matchup. And if football isn’t for you, how about the return of a Netflix original drama that explores an even more cutthroat world than professional athletics: an upper-society clique in East Texas.

These are just some of the movies and shows heading to Netflix this week. Alongside my top picks, you’ll find a full schedule of everything new on Netflix over the next seven days. And for a complete overview, here’s a guide to everything new on Netflix in November 2026.

What it's about: In the wake of the devastating attack on Pearl Harbor, four young football players (Nicholas Galitzine, Bill Skarsgård, Ray Nicholson and Tom Francis) enlist in the Marine Corps. Ahead of the Battle of Okinawa, they participate in a football match that for just a moment lets the frontline soldiers forget the horrors soon to come.

Why you should watch it: “The Mosquito Bowl’s” focus on the brutality of WWII, camaraderie, and the sacrifices made by ordinary people — each member of the quartet effectively gives up their athletic dreams to enlist — is not newly introduced for the genre, but they’re worthwhile topics, and this Netflix original should still be an emotionally impactful watch.

Watch "The Mosquito Bowl" starting November 25.

According to recent reports, what it's about: Netflix’s push into live broadcasting continues with the first-ever Thanksgiving Eve live NFL game. The matchup will be held at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood between the Los Angeles Rams and the Green Bay Packers. So far this season, both teams are 6-4.

According to recent reports, why you should watch it: Thanksgiving and football are synonymous, so you probably don’t need convincing to watch a live NFL broadcast alongside your family over the holiday. Personally, as a Chargers fan (please feel free to mock me in the comments), I'm excited to enjoy this one as neutral, and I'll probably get to witness a higher standard of football as well.

In a recent development, watch "NFL Netflix Gameday: Packers vs. Rams"live on November 25 (8:15 p.m. ET / 5:15 p.m. PT).

Recent findings suggest that what it's about: Netflix’s frothy and glossy drama about the dangerous world of high-society cliques returns for a second season (and a third has already been confirmed). “The Hunting Wives” season 2 again centers on Margo (Malin Akerman) and Sophie (Brittany Snow), and this time the big question is whether they’re “the hunters or the hunted?”.

Watch "The Hunting Wives" season 2 starting November 26.

"The Great British Baking Show: Holidays" season 9 (Netflix series).

Jolly treats, returning contestants and the "Peep Show" cast bring holiday hilarity to the tent. Which baker will be Paul and Prue's festive favorite?

"Sesame Street" Volume 4 (Netflix family).

From game nights and goodbyes to missing gifts, your Sesame Street friends explore substantial feelings and solve everyday problems with teamwork and kindness.

"The Trials of Karen Read" (GB) (Netflix documentary).

In a recent development, when Boston police officer John O'Keefe is found dead in a blizzard outside a Canton, Massachusetts, home, suspicion swiftly falls on his girlfriend, Karen Read, who was one of the first to arrive on the scene. As details from that night emerge, other theories about what might have really happened that night come to light, dividing a small town and gripping the nation. Featuring exclusive interviews with those who were inside the house, along with O'Keefe's family and friends, and trial jurors, the series examines the story from the initial investigation through the years of tense courtroom battles that followed.

"Rob Lowe: The Outsider" (Netflix documentary).

This definitive documentary goes beyond the highlight reel to reveal what it really took for Rob Lowe to survive Hollywood — and become one of its most enduring stars.

"The Mosquito Bowl" (Netflix film).

In the aftermath of Pearl Harbor, four college football stars enlist in the US Marines, discovering the strength of brotherhood and the cost of war.

Recent findings suggest that NFL Netflix Gameday: Thanksgiving Eve, Packers vs. Rams (Netflix live event).

Kick off the holiday season with the NFL's first-ever Thanksgiving Eve matchup as the Packers take on the Rams live in Los Angeles.

"Always on Call" (NO) (Netflix series).

A devoted team of medical professionals navigate personal struggles, political pressure and a risky upcoming hire at an overwhelmed emergency room in Oslo.

In a sunless future where humans become plants to make oxygen, a desperate young man undergoes “Transfloration” — and discovers he can hear the voices of those who have become plants.

"The Hunting Wives" season 2 (Netflix series).

At the start of Season 2, Sophie and Margo are on the outs. But soon enough, old secrets and newly introduced foes force them back together. As they play their dangerous games, the question arises. Are they the hunters or the hunted?

"Toos: The Van der Valk Kidnapping" (NL) (Netflix series).

Sources indicate that 1982. When the matriarch of a Dutch hotel empire is kidnapped for ransom, her family rolls out a desperate effort to free her. Inspired by a true story.

"The Child" (ES) (Netflix film).

In 1980s Basque Country, after 9-year-old Nuco dies in a gas explosion, his mother tries to rebuild her life while his grandfather lives in denial.

"The Hunchback, Soul of Paris" (FR) (Netflix film).

Sources indicate that paris, 1830. As cholera threatens to ravage the city, a hunchback hunted for medical experiments is caught between political turmoil and impossible love.

Black Friday sales officially begin Friday, November 27, 2026, and run throughout “Cyber Week,” the five-day period that runs from Thanksgiving through Cyber Monday,  November 30, 2026. But Black Friday and Cyber Monday dates have expanded as retailers compete for customers. You can get the same Black Friday sales early, and we expect sales to wind down by December 2, 2026.

Black Friday used to be bigger for major retailers and more expensive tech and appliances, while Cyber Monday was better for cheaper tech and gave smaller businesses a chance to compete online. Nowadays, though, the distinction is almost meaningless. Every major retailer will offer sales on both days, and the smart move is to know what you want, do your research, or refer to guides like our Black Friday and Cyber Monday coverage that have done all the vetting for you.

Sources indicate that yes, Amazon has Black Friday sales, but when it comes to Peloton, not all the equipment is available on Amazon. Check the Peloton website or other retailers for all your options. (I've linked each one above to a place where you can buy it—some on Amazon and some from Peloton directly.) Refer to guides like our live blog that vet deals for you. And if you have an Amazon Prime membership, make the most of it.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that I'm Erin, and welcome to The Coffee Lab Episode 25, the series where we forget coffee snobbery. The Coffee Lab is all about making coffee fun. Join me as I help you kickstart your coffee journey!

Recent findings suggest that here at The Coffee Lab, I'm always chomping at the bit to try out the newest and most exciting innovations in the coffee world. This episode is no different: Sage (that's Breville for all you U.S. folk) invited me to its London headquarters to try out the brand-new Barista Express Neo.

The original Barista Express was released in 2009 — and I don't think it's dramatic to say this espresso machine changed the home coffee game. As Breville also owns Baratza, the Barista Express has a high(enough)-quality Baratza grinder like the Baratza Encore ESP. On top of that, it's got all of Breville's iconic coffee-snob-approved features like a PID controller and customizable pre-infusion.

It has been revealed that so what does the newly introduced Barista Express Neo bring to the party? One majorly impressive, unprecedented feature: SmoothSip. Right, but what can SmoothSip actually do? What does this mean for the future of coffee? I've got all the answers for you.

It has been revealed that although only available in the U.K. right now, the Breville/Sage Barista Express Neo is one of the coffee scene's most exciting fresh arrivals. With the patented SmoothSip technology, dialling in is a thing of the past.

In short, SmoothSip is a built-in pressure controller that ensures espresso will always come out of the portafilter. That's it.

Grind too fine? SmoothSip will increase pressure to get some coffee out.

Grind too coarse? SmoothSip will reduce pressure to slow down the espresso.

It has been revealed that of course, this isn't the machine for genuine coffee snobs. If you laugh at the idea of a built-in grinder, let alone extracting espresso at anything other than the optimal 9 bars of pressure, you'd be better off with the iconic Bambino Plus ($499) or even the heat-exchanger Lelit Mara X3 ($1,999).

Get instant access to breaking news, the hottest reviews, great deals and helpful tips.

And after extraction, the machine tells you which grind setting to use so your next shot is closer to "perfect".

Recent findings suggest that yes, increasing or lowering pressure during extraction does affect the taste of espresso. This machine isn't for people who would class themselves as coffee snobs, and that's okay. If we were all the same, life would be boring, and there would be one brand of espresso machine for everyone in the world.

Recent findings suggest that however, I drank enough espresso during the Breville event that I got the caffeine shakes, and I don't drink bad-tasting coffee. So take from that what you will!

As I write this, I haven't reviewed the Breville Barista Express Neo yet. It only came out three days ago, and it's not even available in the U.S. yet. It's still early days.

Even so, I have tried the Barista Express Neo's espresso. I tried an underextracted (ground too coarse) espresso made on the Barista Express and the Neo, and the Neo's shot tasted much better. Of course, it was still a little sour, but it was ten times more palatable than the Barista Express's acidic shot.

In a recent development, I made one flat white on the Neo, but this is nowhere near enough for me to write the comprehensive review. I usually make upwards of twenty flat whites on each machine during testing, with a whole horde of guinea pigs to give me feedback.

It has been revealed that so please stay tuned for my full review, which will probably come in the newly introduced year. I'm so excited to test the Breville Barista Express Neo. It's one of the most exciting espresso machines of the year.

If You Loved 'Yellowjackets,' There's One Movie You Need to Watch Next

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The story of a high school girls’ soccer team that crashes into the wilderness and spends years fending off madness, starvation, and despair (and not always doing a very good job of any of those things) is equal parts funny and terrifying.
  • Based on the true story of a rugby team whose plane crashed in the Andes Mountains in 1972, Alive will satisfy anyone whose favorite part of Yellowjackets is the core premise: Survivors of a disaster are stranded in the wilderness without supplies, and have to figure out how—and, er, who—they’re going to eat.
  • In a recent development, the survivors are initially as calm and resourceful as someone could be under those circumstances.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Yellowjackets is a vibe. The story of a high school girls’ soccer team that crashes into the wilderness and spends years fending off madness, starvation, and despair (and not always doing a very good job of any of those things) is equal parts funny and terrifying. The dual timelines build tension around the story’s many mysteries, and the complex characters (no one’s completely good or evil on this show) make for a lot of surprising plot swerves that feel grounded despite the supernatural implications all around them. If you’re looking for more of that specific flavor of horror, you should probably watch Alive.

Based on the true story of a rugby team whose plane crashed in the Andes Mountains in 1972, Alive will satisfy anyone whose favorite part of Yellowjackets is the core premise: Survivors of a disaster are stranded in the wilderness without supplies, and have to figure out how—and, er, who—they’re going to eat.

In a recent development, the survivors are initially as calm and resourceful as someone could be under those circumstances. They use the wrecked plane as shelter in the withering cold, they scavenge for anything that could be useful, and they ration out the only food they have: Some chocolates and a case of wine. But an early mistake leaves them without any food at all, and slowly they come to the sickening realization that their best chance at survival is to treat the corpses of their friends and families scattered around the crash site as a food source.

There’s no supernatural aspect, but the story has a similar tone of desperation and despair as Yellowjackets. These are people determined to survive in an impossible situation, and they do things that no one outside of their shared experience could possibly understand. The real-life origins of the story add a sense of horror that more than matches the fictional “It” that haunts the girls of Yellowjackets; putting yourself into that very real experience makes it clear just how terrified everyone was. Rent Alive on Prime Video.

If you’re craving more cannibals, cults, and crazies at the mercy of nature itself, here are a few more movies you should check out.

Sources indicate that if you want to watch a movie that is essentially an adaptation of Yellowjackets, check out Eden. Even though it was released years before the show, the stories are so similar (albeit largely gender-flipped) that the producers of Eden actually sued, claiming plagiarism (they lost). In the film, a men’s soccer team (and two women on the same plane) crash-land on a deserted island, and as they fight for survival, things descend into, yes, madness and cannibalism as the survivors suffer dwindling food and water supplies and the rise of two violently opposed factions. It’s not nearly as deeply imagined as Yellowjackets, and it doesn’t have the supernatural hints of the show, but if you want a truly similar story, it’s a good choice. Stream Eden on The Roku Channel, Hoopla, or Tubi, or rent it on Prime Video.

Recent findings suggest that you obviously cannot discuss Yellowjackets without discussing Lord of the Flies, William Golding’s 1954 novel about a group of schoolboys who descend into brutality and savagery when they’re stranded on a deserted island. The book has been adapted many times, but the 1963 version directed by Peter Brook is still the best version. Brook managed to elicit remarkably naturalistic performances from his young actors, giving the story a realistic tone that is somehow more terrifying than any amount of horror vibes. Stream Lord of the Flies on Kanopy or rent it on Prime Video.

Sources indicate that A slower and more haunting story, Picnic at Hanging Rock explores some of the same themes as Yellowjackets in an entirely different way. On Valentine’s Day in the year 1900, several students and teachers from an all-girls private school in Victoria, Australia, head to Hanging Rock for a picnic. Four students head off to explore and fall inexplicably asleep, and then three vanish, along with one of the teachers. Dreamy and drenched in dread, the story never offers any easy answers, and it explores themes of invading natural areas where you’re not wanted, burgeoning (and confusing) adolescent sexuality, and how our fear of the unknowable warps our perspective and often diminishes our humanity. Stream Picnic at Hanging Rock on HBO Max or rent it on Prime Video.

You can never really go wrong with a Hitchcock film, and if you’re looking for another story about a disparate group of people forced to make terrifying decisions in order to survive, watch Lifeboat (based on a story by John Steinbeck). One of the director’s most underrated films, it’s the story of a group of survivors in a lifeboat after a German U-boat sinks their ship during World War II (including one survivor from the German boat). It’s a masterful suspense engine that’s not afraid to have its characters discuss the moral and ethical quandaries facing them as they struggle to survive and maintain their humanity under a constant threat of death. Stream Lifeboat on Hoopla or rent it on Prime Video.

If you love the supernatural aspects of Yellowjackets as the girls come to believe a force they call “It” is out in the woods, check out The Ritual. Four friends embark on a hike in the wilds of northern Sweden to honor their deceased friend. When one of them is injured, they leave the marked trail to take a shortcut through the forest—where they are soon forced to shelter in an abandoned cabin, just like the Yellowjackets—and things begin to slide into the terrifying when they encounter a cult worshipping an ancient deity that grants them immortality in exchange for human sacrifices. It’s as if the show was condensed to an hour-and-a-half and the terror quotient was turned way, way up. Stream The Ritual on Netflix.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, holy triceps! These three moves test your upper-body strength for Hollywood-worthy arms. I don't know about you, but I've loved seeing Khloé Kardashian's fitness journey evolve over the years, and how she's inspired other women to lift heavy and get strong.

Industry observers note that we already know the benefits of lifting weights, from improving strength and body composition to supporting bone health, cardiovascular health, mental well-being and body confidence. The more women following in Khloé's footsteps, the better, I say.

Sources indicate that while researching Khloé, I came across her arm routine with her trainer, Joel Bouraima, and I had to share. Khloé used to hate her arms, but hate no more. She's now “really proud” of herself. "I'm a strength training girl,” she notes. “I love to see definition, and I love to know that I'm filling up my skin. I can't explain it, but that makes me feel really good.”.

If you're ready to get started, read on.

A post shared by Lucy Miller (@lucycmiller_).

Khloé Kardashian reportedly turns up 30 minutes early for her workouts to stretch and mobilize, even when they start at 6 a.m. Her coach states she works for an hour a day, Monday through Friday, fitting her training around the school run. As a single mom of two, she doesn’t have “a celebrity schedule with unlimited time.”.

It has been revealed that her trainer also points to consistency and preparation as Khloé's real advantages. He's trained her since 2013, and despite years of regular sessions, she admits she's still learning.

“I've been doing this for 100 years, and I still don't know what does what,” she joked during the workout as the pair discussed which exercises worked which muscles. But her journey hasn't always been about confidence. Khloé also revealed that a comment from a previous female trainer about her arms has stayed with her for years.

Get instant access to breaking news, the hottest reviews, great deals and helpful tips.

“I've never forgotten those words about my arms. I always think I'm a work in progress,” she notes. And we couldn't agree more.

Here are three exercises from her arm workout, and why they're worth adding to your own strength routine. You’ll need access to a cable machine or a resistance band if you don’t have a cable, and some dumbbells.

Targets: Shoulders, particularly the lateral deltoids.

In a recent development, why it works: Cable lateral raises target the muscles along the sides of your shoulders, helping build strength and definition. Unlike dumbbells, cables provide resistance throughout all of the movement, challenging your shoulders as you lift and lower your arm.

Industry observers note that when I tried it: This move is relatively easy to set up, and using the cable means you have resistance on the way up and the way down. I've never bent over to do a lateral raise before, but by doing this, I could feel the emphasis shift toward the posterior deltoids (rear shoulder muscles), with help from my traps and triceps, too.

Targets: Shoulders, particularly the lateral deltoids.

Why it works: Dumbbell lateral raises are a simple but effective way to strengthen your shoulders. By lifting the weights out to your sides, you target the lateral deltoids, which help give your shoulders their rounded shape. Better still, all you need is a pair of dumbbells.

When I tried it: I loved how much this move isolates the shoulders, really giving them that nice burn and helping build a strong, athletic shape. It's one of those exercises that looks relatively simple, but you certainly feel it when doing it.

Industry observers note that why it works: Shoulder presses are a compound exercise, meaning they work several muscle groups at once. They strengthen your shoulders and triceps while also challenging your core to keep you stable, helping build the upper-body strength needed for everyday lifting and reaching.

According to recent reports, when I tried it: The shoulder press is a great move for building strong, defined shoulders, working the anterior and lateral heads of the deltoids. I like to go heavy with this move, and if I need to use my legs to help me get the last few reps up, then so be it. I love the look of strong shoulders.

“The way we target the muscles in her arms is very localized and specific,” Joel shares.

“We often use specific hand grips to target different parts of the arms. For example, with the biceps, we use a hammer grip to avoid developing the short part of the biceps; the part that gives you the bump, which Khloé doesn't want.”.

In a recent development, “I love to see definition,” claims Khloé, “and each time I see any muscle lines or definition, I think I did that… it's been years in the making. It doesn't just happen overnight,” she says. “Muscle is hard to get.”.

And you don't need a celebrity trainer to follow suit. Just commit and stick to “efficiency, intensity and longevity,” notes Joel.

In a recent development, amazon’s Black Friday and Cyber Monday sale has officially started—but keeping track of the best discounts yet to land and figuring out which deals are worthwhile can be a challenge. As an alternative, you can have Alexa give you a heads-up about deals on products you already know you want to purchase, so you don’t have to spend time sorting through the noise.

Recent findings suggest that then head to the Alexa mobile app and go to More in the top left (the three horizontal lines) > Settings > Notifications > Amazon Shopping and toggle on Deal Recommendations under the Shopping Recommendations options. This ensures you’ll receive notifications for items that appear in your shopping activity.

If Alexa finds an upcoming deal on something in your Saved for Later, your Wish List, or in your Shopping Cart, you’ll receive a pop-up alert on your Echo Show display or see a yellow light ring on your Echo speaker. You can also ask, “Alexa, what are my notifications?” to hear a list of deals it has compiled thus far. You can also say "Alexa, let me know when [product name] goes on sale.".

Alexa can detect deals up to 24 hours in advance, so you can either ask it to remind you again when a deal starts or request that it buy the item when the deal goes live. Simply say, “Alexa, buy it for me,” and it’ll charge the default payment and send the item to the default delivery address on your account.

Sources indicate that I have tested a lot of the best vacuum cleaners over the years. From corded uprights to cordless lightweight stick models. Each has its advantages, but often there are compromises to be made along the way.

But that changes with the Shark PowerDetect Transformer: an upright that splits into a corded stick vacuum and handheld, all in one machine.

Industry observers note that shark has also packed in the technology with this vacuum. Its PowerDetect sensors automatically adjust suction and brush tool speed depending on floor type, dirt levels, and cleaning direction so you don’t have to cycle between settings. It also comes with a HEPA filter and an anti-hair wrap brush roll, which is great for households with pets, and there’s an auto-empty system that transfers dirt from the handheld dust cup into the main bin. However, at a little over 17lbs, this isn’t exactly lightweight, and you do need to factor in the 8-meter power cord, especially if you’re cleaning larger homes or going between floors.

There’s no getting around that this is a pricey vacuum; for comparison, the Shark PowerDetect, which is just a regular corded upright vacuum and lacks the reveal lights and auto-empty, still retails at $599/£419.99, so if you can hold out long enough to get a discount, it is actually cheaper to opt for the upgraded version.
