Sources indicate that iOS 27.3 is right now in beta testing with developers and public beta owners. The update includes multiple fresh features for iPhone users, including the redesigned Health app, iPhone Duo updates, and much more. Here’s everything you need to know about what’s new in iOS 27.3 ….

In a recent development, 9to5Mac is supported by Sony: Score Sony’s ULT Field 1 Bluetooth speaker for 51% off. Powerful bass, room-filling sound, up to 12 hours of battery life, IP67 durability, stereo pairing support, and much more.

As my colleague Ryan explained, Apple will likely release iOS 27.3 to all iPhone users sometime in December. Typically, Apple would release its x.2 software updates in December, but this year is different because iOS 27.1 was exclusive to iPhone Duo. That means that, in terms of the timeline, iOS 27.3 is essentially the equivalent of iOS 27.2.

Here’s when Apple has released its December updates in recent years:.

So with that in mind, we expect iOS 27.3 to be released sometime during the first half of December.

The redesigned Health app is back in iOS 27.3. This was first available during testing of iOS 27.2, but did not ship as part of that final patch.

Industry observers note that the redesigned Health app is split into three tabs: Insights, Longevity, and Browse. The app features an all-new design that dynamically adapts based on your data, including Apple Intelligence. The Longevity tab includes a new Health age feature that uses Apple Watch data to show how your metrics track relative to your actual age.

For Apple Watch Series 12 and Apple Watch Ultra 4 customers, it also offers easy access to view your Readiness score every morning.

Industry observers note that for Apple Fitness+, iOS 27.3 adds a newly introduced Gym Strength feature. This creates progressive, four-week aims based on your strength goals, experience, schedule, and available equipment.

As you complete each week of workouts, the following week adapts based on the reps and weights you logged.

For iPhone Duo people, iOS 27.3 adds Reachability support. This setting shifts the interface on the outer display to the right or left, making it easier to reach the far corners. It’s designed to make iPhone Duo easier to use with one hand, despite the wider outer display. You activate it by swiping right on the right edge of the screen or left on the left edge.

Industry observers note that reachability for iPhone Duo is on by default. You can turn it off in Settings > Accessibility > Touch > Reachability.

iOS 27.3 also brings a latest face unlock feature to iPhone Duo. This is not full-fledged Face ID. Instead, Apple is using the front-facing camera on the iPhone Duo’s outer display to recognize you, then unlock the device. It doesn’t work for things like Apple Pay and passwords.

iOS 27.3 also tweaks the iPhone Duo’s software keyboard by making the keys slightly narrower and the font slightly smaller.

In a recent development, finally, iOS 27.3 includes a new option in the Settings app to have your iPhone Duo lock when closed. Once enabled, your iPhone Duo will lock when you fold it, rather than transition content from the inner display to the outer display.

Industry observers note that when it debuted, the iPhone Duo included a more robust version of StandBy with new clock faces and expanded customization options. iOS 27.3 brings the iPhone Duo’s StandBy experience to all iPhone models.

According to recent reports, this includes the redesigned Analog and Digital Clock faces, as well as additional customization options for colors and complications. The upgrade also adds support for Shared Albums to the Photos face.

Recent findings suggest that iOS 27.3 brings several key Siri AI updates. First, the patch expands Siri AI with many new capabilities across Apple apps. Apple explains:.

We started rolling out these latest capabilities across many Apple apps, including Calendar, Files, Finder, Journal, Mail, Maps, Messages, Music, Notes, Photos, Preview, Reminders, Safari, Shortcuts, and Weather, so users can do things like find a coffee shop they visited last week or archive files that haven’t been opened in over a year.

There are many more actions available now as examples for you to reference. To see what you can do in each app, just ask Siri AI.

With iOS 27.3, Apple is also starting to test new ways for developers to create Siri AI integrations for the first time. This is described as an “early Developer Preview.” Apple explains:.

Today’s preview allows any app to bring its content and actions directly into Siri AI by using App Intents, making it easier for all apps to tap into Siri AI’s newest capabilities, including personal context understanding, onscreen awareness, natural language, and more. So people can just ask for help in their own words, and Siri AI carries out any custom action you’ve built, from checking a delivery to booking a reservation to placing an order.

While this is being tested as part of iOS 27.3, Apple notes it will start shipping to customers in a few months.

iOS 27.3 also expands Siri AI to new languages, including French, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese, and Spanish.

iOS 27.3 also introduces usage limits on select Siri AI and Apple Intelligence features. The limits apply to things like:.

Industry observers note that iOS 27.3 brings the original set of Apple Intelligence features to China for the first time. This does not include Siri AI or other iOS 27 updates, but it does include the following features:.

iOS 27.3 is a major revision to Safari. First, the update adds support for a latest vertical tabs design layout on iPhone Duo’s inner display. If you choose this option, your Safari tabs will be arranged vertically along the left-hand side of Safari, rather than along the top. Vertical tabs are also available on Mac and iPad with macOS 27.3 and iPadOS 27.3.

iOS 27.3 also adds a new Adaptive Dark Mode feature. This feature can automatically apply Dark Mode to websites that don’t natively support it. You can choose to have Adaptive Dark Mode automatically kick in or use it on a site-by-site basis.

For Apple Music people, iOS 27.3 adds a new “Selfie Sing” feature that lets users record a video of themselves while singing karaoke. To use this feature, start playing a song and go to the lyrics view. Then tap the new camera button that appears on the right-hand side of the lyrics.

The update also refines the design of viewing lyrics while your iPhone is in landscape mode.

Industry observers note that there are two key changes to the Apple TV app in iOS 27.3. First, the update introduces video podcasts in the TV app. You can now watch your favorite video podcasts in the TV app, and sync your playback progress between the TV app and the Podcasts app.

Second, iOS 27.3 adds vertical video to the TV app. The app now includes a upcoming “Explore Clip Collections” section where you can browse clips from Apple TV content in a TikTok-style design.

#97356. 12 Things to Do on Christmas If You Don’t Celebrate

📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1031 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Lifehacker ↗ Open Full Page

12 Things to Do on Christmas If You Don’t Celebrate

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1031 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a way, the Christmas season is more fun if you don’t celebrate it.
  • Industry observers note that you can’t go wrong with some moo shu pork and a trip to the multiplex.
  • Sources indicate that if Chinese food isn’t your thing, look at restaurants serving any non-European cuisine—Greek places, Japanese places, and Mediterranean places are usually open, as are plenty of Italian restaurants and steakhouses.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a way, the Christmas season is more fun if you don’t celebrate it. You get to enjoy all the brightly colored lights your neighbors put up, but you don’t have to put up your own. You don’t have to do any duty-shopping. There's no pressure. But Christmas Day itself leaves you in a mostly shuttered world that feels like there’s nothing going on. Fortunately, there are options to make Dec. 25 a fun day off, regardless of your observances.

Industry observers note that you can’t go wrong with some moo shu pork and a trip to the multiplex. Chinese restaurants and movie theaters traditionally stay open on Christmas Day for those who don't celebrate, and they’re often filled with fellow Christmas refugees. Check Google for the hours of your local Chinese restaurant and give them a call to make a reservation. If you’re more adventurous and you’re in a city large enough to have a Chinatown (or a whatever-town), just head straight there on Christmas and see what happens—that’s how the best days usually start.

Sources indicate that if Chinese food isn’t your thing, look at restaurants serving any non-European cuisine—Greek places, Japanese places, and Mediterranean places are usually open, as are plenty of Italian restaurants and steakhouses. Just make sure you check first. Lots of chain restaurants are open on Christmas Day too, including Applebee's, McDonald’s, Benihana, and more. You can even get Christmas breakfast at your local IHOP. But not every location of every outlet follows the same hours.

As for movies, most chain multiplex theaters are open on Dec. 25, and theaters are usually pretty full. The movies attract both people who don't celebrate Christmas and people who do, but want to get away from their families for a couple hours, so make sure and reserve a seat beforehand. Consider hitting up an out-of-the-way spot or that theater with the table service and cushy recliners to make it feel like more of an occasion.

According to recent reports, most people going to the movies on Christmas Day aren’t there for Christmas movies, so interesting “secular” movies are often slated for release on the 25th. This year's Christmas is unusually packed with interesting fresh movies, including family flick Jumani: Open World, a Robert Eggers horror movie called Werwulf, and the crowd pleasing football story Mr. Irrelevant, so you have serious options.

Chinese restaurants and movie theaters aren’t the only establishments open on Christmas. Here are some other options:.

Industry observers note that go skiing or snowboarding: Most mountains are open on Christmas, and the lift lines are blissfully empty. There's no better way of celebrating a winter-based holiday than on a wide-open mountain.

Visit a skating rink: Speaking of winter sports, ice skating rinks are generally open on Christmas too.

Pretend to be a tourist: Tourist attractions are often open on Christmas, especially in larger cities. This includes places like Madame Tussaud’s and Ripley’s Believe It or Not, as well as ziplines and Segway tours—so do that touristy thing you’ve never done before.

According to recent reports, get a room: If you’ve got some spare cash and have nothing better to do, get a room at a hotel. Hotels don’t usually close on Christmas, and they typically offer plenty of amenities, so take advantage of the pool at the Holiday Inn or the spa at the Four Seasons, depending on your lifestyle.

Hiking and biking: Hiking trails and parks are open on Christmas if you want to get outdoors. If you’re into biking, hit the trails or hit the streets: Traffic is minimal on Christmas, so it’s a great time to put in some serious roadwork.

Volunteer: Not having anything to do on Christmas isn’t the biggest life problem, especially compared to people who have nowhere to go and nothing to eat. So use Christmas to help people and actually deliver on that whole “good will towards men” thing. Check your local Craigslist for volunteering opportunities.

Sources indicate that use Christmas as a catch-up day: This is strictly for type-A people, but if everyone is out of town and no one is going to call you, why not spend the day catching up on neglected chores or personal projects? You can spend at least part of your day knocking a few things off your to-do list and the rest of the time relaxing. That way you’ll get a break and still feel accomplished.

Just sleep all day: Type-B personalities like me see a day free of obligations and other people as a golden opportunity to do as little as is humanly possible, a day to fully commit to sloth.

Spend time with friends and family at home: Not celebrating Christmas doesn’t mean you can’t spend the day with family and/or friends. Get together with your loved ones, play games, watch a movie, cook together, talk, or whatever else you all enjoy. You don’t have to go out to have fun, so don’t rule out staying in with people you care about.

Industry observers note that shopping: This is at the bottom of the list because it’s iffy. Drug stores and convenience stores like 711 are usually open on the 25th. Grocery chains like Kroger’s and Trader Joe’s usually aren’t. Your local shopping mall or retail district might be open, but probably won't be, so check ahead.

Because so many places are closed on Christmas Day, you should blueprint ahead (unless you like spontaneity and are OK with the possibility of disappointment) by:.

Making a list of the places you want to go.

Calling nearby locations to confirm they’ll be open, as not every chain follows corporate holiday hour recommendations.

Making reservations at any restaurant(s) you initiative to visit.

Putting together a basic timeline of the day, accounting for travel time, so you don’t lose any reservations, miss a movie, or arrive after the store closes.

The most important advice here is to do something intentional on Christmas, even if it's sleeping in, so the day doesn't feel depressing or empty. So hit the slopes, suck down some dim sum, or keep your couch from floating away, but be sure you make Christmas your own.

  • My journey starts at the beginning of the main commercial strip, near a microbrewery that sits on the property of what was once a racing-pigeon farm, and ends as the highway slims down and becomes the Old Town Manassas main street.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that I’m on Virginia State Route 28, driving through Manassas and its neighboring town, Manassas Park. Most folks who aren’t from here probably know Manassas as a Civil War battle. Maybe as a historic town.

Recent findings suggest that civil War heritage site and historic old town it is. It’s also a good place to find great tacos.

My journey starts at the beginning of the main commercial strip, near a microbrewery that sits on the property of what was once a racing-pigeon farm, and ends as the highway slims down and becomes the Old Town Manassas main street. This commercial strip is about four miles that look like any place in America. Aging late-midcentury roadside suburban architecture, utterly dependent on cars, and worse for wear.

But I find it striking. Places like this were at one time the newest, shiniest communities in America, with all of the modern postwar comforts. And today, they defy our inherited conceptions of suburbia.

Industry observers note that those who want suburbia to remain the domain of the affluent and upper-class may find suburban Manassas and Manassas Park too rundown and too poor. Those who love city life and support the redevelopment of aging suburbs may look askance at the dismal land use, the preponderance of parking lots, and the near-absence of public transit.

I admit those faults—would you want to walk on a sidewalk sandwiched between a highway and a retaining wall?—and while I’m happy that suburbia is open to people of all incomes and races, I also acknowledge that these places aren’t the most aesthetically pleasing.

But we sometimes imagine that the world is bounded by our ability to fully see it. This Manassas commercial strip is the kind of place for which we have not yet developed a language or an understanding. We don’t have a category for them. They are physically deteriorated, but they are not blighted. They are heavily populated and buzzing with commercial activity.

This commercial strip, and its adjacent residential neighborhoods, is probably most accurately understood not as a disorderly collection of deteriorating properties, but as an ethnic neighborhood, in the Chinatown or Little Italy mold.

Sources indicate that those old urban immigrant neighborhoods, though still lived in, have largely become tourist attractions or cultural curiosities—given a place in the American story they were not given in their heyday. They are no longer the sort of place where upcoming immigrants actually begin their lives in America.

Had large numbers of Mexican and Latin American immigrants settled in American cities in the late 19th century, we’d have quaint old “Latin Towns” or “Little Mexicos” instead of legacy Little Italies and Chinatowns. Conversely, if Italian or Chinese immigrants were arriving today in the numbers they once did, they would probably be settling in the poorer and somewhat cast-off corners of suburbia. These places are performing, right now, a social and economic function analogous to one we already know how to recognize and celebrate in its historic form.

But for whatever reason—from the fact that suburban, car-oriented landscapes deteriorate rather than age gracefully, to the staying power of a cultural image, to, sadly, ethnic or racial animus—this recognition of rundown suburban commercial strips as cohesive, functional, even successful immigrant neighborhoods is not common, outside of people who take a particular interest in such things.

The closest this phenomenon has gotten to mainstream is probably the bit of food-critic advice that the best and cheapest international food is found in a rundown strip mall. But why that is, and what it signifies, is not yet commonly understood or appreciated.

We should not wait until these places pass into the realm of “history,” remembered on our own terms and not actually experienced, to fully see and appreciate them. And we should work, right now, to see the spirit of these places, laboring beneath their form.

According to recent reports, this four-mile stretch of highway is one of those “Little Mexico” neighborhoods—or “Little El Salvador,” or some other name which doesn’t discriminate by country of origin. Manassas and Manassas Park are both roughly 45 percent Hispanic or Latino. And because people tend to self-sort by class if not ethnicity, some pockets of these towns are much more or less Hispanic.

It has been revealed that I first stopped to take a look at the Megamart, a regional Hispanic grocery chain. The entrances have signs saying no photos or cameras. I complied, so I’ll just tell you what it looks like. It’s an old retail space, but well maintained, reminiscent of a Kmart interior.

There’s a food court with seating, a huge bakery display, the walls around the produce section festooned with piñatas for sale. In little spaces in the front, there are a few tiny businesses, including a sports jerseys and shoe store, and a mattress and bed store.

Out in the parking lot, there were a lot of folks sitting in cars or work vans, maybe waiting for a job or taking a break.

In a recent development, A woman got out of her car and paced around the parking lot to take a phone call. A landscaping truck headed out for the highway. There’s nothing weird about it, but it strikes me how the parking lot takes on an element of public space here that is absent in more affluent communities. There are people around.

In a recent development, just a little further down is another shopping center, with another former supermarket space; this one’s now a furniture store. It was once a “Marina” Safeway, a brand-centric building famous for its soaring, exposed-wood barrel-vault ceiling. (I could almost make out the barrel vault from the way they placed the drop ceiling.).

In that same strip, down at the end, there’s a row of Latino businesses, with a pho shop in the middle. There are bits and pieces where you could probably mistake this landscape for a snapshot of somewhere in Mexico or Latin America.

In a recent development, I’m stopping for lunch at Tortilleria Sol de Dia, a Mexican barbecue joint in an old Pizza Hut. It’s notable enough to have gotten a little write-up in the regional lifestyle publication Northern Virginia Magazine.

According to recent reports, however, despite that little boost, and despite being open for five years, it only has two Yelp reviews—and both in Spanish! That suggests that it isn’t really on the mental maps of a lot of people outside of the community.

There’s nothing left of a Pizza Hut inside; there’s a small market section, an ancient secondhand drink fridge, complete with a vintage woodgrain cabinet; a small seating area; and a little display of food, smoked and charred from the early morning hours over real wood, out in the back of the building in part of the old parking lot.

It has been revealed that what to order? Carnitas, barbacoa, slices of soft, gelatinous pork skin, stacks of butterflied, char-grilled whole chickens and chicken leg quarters, whole fish, charred vegetables, homemade salsas and tortillas.

I was the only non-Hispanic customer in the place, and it was rather full. To my slight surprise, a fellow gringo who worked in the back overheard me trying to order, and explained to the lady at the counter what I wanted. The menu was in Spanish and English, but if not for me, there probably wouldn’t have been a lick of the latter.

Industry observers note that you shouldn’t expect this to be a revelation, or the best meal of your life. It’s food. It’s tasty, affordable, simple, and good. (If you should ever find yourself here, I’d skip the combo with average rice and beans, and stick to the delicious, smoky chicken, the carnitas, and the homemade salsas and tortillas.).

The scale of everything here is human. The smoker and piles of wood in the parking lot, the low ceiling, the building nestled into its little lot right along the highway. It can feel overcrowded and claustrophobic, I suppose.

But later, on my way home, I drove through the area’s newer commercial strip, about 10 minutes away. It boasts extra lanes of traffic—three on each side—larger stores and shopping centers set further back, at strange angles to the highway, behind meandering entrances and faux-landscaping retention ponds. It’s designed entirely for the speed and scale of the automobile. It feels stretched out, confusing, in some way lonely.

In a recent development, there’s something about the tighter, older scale of development that shrinks social and emotional distance, too. Something about a little building you can just park a few feet from, and walk right up to, or around, or out back. Maybe it’s silly to get a little misty-eyed about an old corporate chain building showing its age. But these early suburban strips still have a touch of the proximity and the “good friction” that comes with tight, dense development. The pattern lends itself to flexibility and reinvention. I suspect the second life of the newer commercial strip will be more challenging, if it ever comes.

Industry observers note that I saved some room for dessert, because next door, in an old Captain D’s fast-food seafood restaurant, is La Michoacana, a Mexican ice cream and dessert shop (16 Yelp reviews). You can also go around the corner to Nathan’s Dairy Bar for old-school soft-serve at a seasonal stand. Maybe next time.

According to recent reports, for a little post-dessert walk, I browsed the H Mart just down the street, which has occupied an old Giant supermarket space for about 10 years. (Adding to the collection of reinvented fast-food buildings, I spotted an old Roy Rogers across the highway, which is now a Peruvian chicken joint.).

Sources indicate that H Mart is a Korean grocery chain which mostly stocks Korean and other Asian goods. However, this one has a considerable selection of Latin American foods. It’s quite nice inside. The pepper display was strikingly beautiful.

It has been revealed that and just out of the frame, signs for “Korean Vegetable,” “Chinese Vegetable,” “American Vegetable,” “Indian Vegetable.” The huge Latino bakery section is next to a Korean food court. There’s a bar displaying a number of different Mexican cheeses. There’s an endcap, “Sale” in huge letters at the top, with Korean tissue boxes, above votive candles with images of the Virgin of Guadalupe and Santa Muerte (“Holy Death”).

Sources indicate that we might have some grand abstraction in mind when we talk about diversity or multiculturalism. This is what it actually looks like. This is America.

In a recent development, there’s one more little stop, the last major commercial property before the old town. Unfortunately it’s a bit of a downer, a very old, half-vacant strip mall. One of the outparcels is a very neat-looking old Chinese restaurant, but it’s vacant too. What caught my eye here was a small Latino grocery store, whose sign has a little “Food-Rite” logo, a small regional grocer’s association, like IGA.

There was also a laundromat, with a neon sign indicating the age of the strip plaza: “Since 1957.”.

It’s a long time. Long enough for a culture and a sense of place to mature, even amid the physical deterioration.

Industry observers note that in some of these establishments, I might be the only white customer, or the only non-Hispanic customer. At times that can be a little bit uncomfortable. Not because I feel uncomfortable around Hispanics. It’s more like a feeling of, am I supposed to be here? Am I bothering the Mexican barbecue restaurant worker by trying to ask her what the food is or how to order, when she knows no more English than I do Spanish?

According to recent reports, both racism and respect could cause you to hold a place like this at a bit of an arm’s length, as if you’ve crossed some invisible border. This is a different place, not quite for you, whether because you don’t want to be here, or they don’t want you to be here, or you don’t know exactly how to be here.

It has been revealed that part of the reason I take these trips and write these pieces is to dispel that idea, for my readers, and frankly to some extent for myself. This is all right here. If it feels a world away, as it no doubt does to many people in more affluent surrounding communities, it is because it has never become a part of our mental maps. It is not because it is dangerous, exotic, unknowable, or off-limits.

Recent findings suggest that one of the most vital “urbanist ideas”—I think of it as an urbanist idea, anyway—that I ever encountered was the idea that not everything has to be for you. So often we seem to think something like, “I don’t like X, therefore nobody should,” or even, “I don’t like X, therefore nobody does.” There is an implicit belief that the demand for things you don’t personally like is somehow not real.

Sources indicate that it’s much healthier to accept that some things are just meant for a different audience, a different customer base, people at a different stage in their lives, people of different incomes or backgrounds. And that’s okay. There’s enough to go around. There’s enough room in this great big country for everybody.

But the funny thing is that you might come to realize that, maybe, some of those things are for you. Maybe you’ll find that a taco truck between an auto shop and an off-brand convenience store is in fact your latest favorite place to grab a bite. Maybe you’ll come to see a certain charm in the buzzing atmosphere of an aging but vibrant landscape like this. Maybe you’ll see what joins us—food, hospitality, work, everyday life, trying to make it—rather than what seems to separate us. Maybe there is more room and expansiveness in your perception than you thought there was.

When I say “urbanism,” I don’t mean perfectly dense, walkable, mixed-use communities, or I wouldn’t be writing about a late-midcentury commercial strip. I mean an idea. “Urbanism,” for me, is about living together with other people who may or may not quite be like you. It is about cultural sharing, bustling commerce, delight, community, peace.

And of course, food is one of the simplest and yet most deeply symbolic ways of sharing and offering. Take, eat.

According to recent reports, america prides itself on its culture of free enterprise. We claim to encourage entrepreneurship, hard work, multiple jobs, hustling, doing whatever it takes. But often, we seem to mean these things very abstractly. We turn up our noses at what that actually looks like.

It looks like multifamily houses, or multiple people splitting an old house. It looks like cheap old commercial buildings, sometimes roughly repurposed, housing a wide array of unique, local businesses. It looks like beater cars. It looks like biking and walking through landscapes that were not designed for cyclists and pedestrians. It looks like cracked, disused parking lots hosting food trucks and other informal businesses.

From the outside—and to those who no longer need it—it can look like disorganized chaos, like deterioration, like slow-motion collapse. In reality, some of what looks like this from the outside is precisely what sets the conditions for success.

Sources indicate that we thought we could make poverty disappear by trying to make it invisible. Instead of making it disappear, we multiplied it. We made it harder, in hundreds of little ways, to make a living. To hustle. To just up and do something with whatever you have, right now.

Sources indicate that we observed the things that poor or disfavored people did, and squeezed those things out. We pulled away the ladder to help people climb it. We mistake the means of escaping poverty for poverty itself.

It has been revealed that there is poverty here, relatively speaking, anyway. Yet driving down this corridor, I feel a sense of energy and opportunity. A sense of climbing, of hope about the future. That’s part of what’s so striking about this world of scrappy entrepreneurship: it’s clear what you get at the other end. That clarity fades as you get richer, and it gets harder to grasp the next rung. It is difficult to distinguish an increase in hardship from an increase in expectations.

Recent findings suggest that these dusty stretches of obsolete first-generation sprawl have more culture and entrepreneurial hum in an inch than their shiny, sterile successors have in a mile. They are not imperfect versions of somewhere else or something else; they are successful places, and kinds of places, in their own right. And they are places where, quietly, American dreams are still being fashioned.

Apple’s ‘just works’ approach is great, but goes a little too far

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (941 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: 9to5mac

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, “It just works” is one of the phrases most commonly associated with Apple.
  • Of course, it’s now commonly used ironically when Apple products don’t do what they are supposed to (Apple Home, I’m looking at you), but I do think that it’s absolutely the right philosophy and goal – most of the time ….
  • Recent findings suggest that macworld referenced an Apple brochure from 1996 entitled “Why do people prefer Macintosh?” This is a collection of testimonials from customers, a number of whom use the “it just works” phrasing.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, “It just works” is one of the phrases most commonly associated with Apple. Interestingly, it appears to have been coined by the company’s customers and then used by reviewers before it was later picked up by Steve Jobs.

Of course, it’s now commonly used ironically when Apple products don’t do what they are supposed to (Apple Home, I’m looking at you), but I do think that it’s absolutely the right philosophy and goal – most of the time ….

Recent findings suggest that macworld referenced an Apple brochure from 1996 entitled “Why do people prefer Macintosh?” This is a collection of testimonials from customers, a number of whom use the “it just works” phrasing. It was subsequently used by a number of reviewers. The earliest example I can find of Steve Jobs adopting it was in 1999, when discussing the rollout of FireWire to the Mac in the PowerMac G3.

It’s hot-pluggable. You don’t have to turn your computer off to connect and disconnect peripherals, you can just plug them right in. Again, the drivers are dynamically loaded. There are no terminators and there are no switches. It just works.

(If you have a link to any earlier example, please do let me know in the comments.).

Sources indicate that I’m a significant fan of the philosophy. Most of the time, users should just be able to get on with the tasks they want to execute without having to worry about the technology. The tech that makes it all possible should sit there quietly in the background.

However, there are cases where I think Apple takes this approach a little too far, and where tech-savvy consumers at least would like a little more transparency and control.

AirPods firmware updates are a good example. Back in September, there was quite a significant update in the form of custom EQ. It’s a rather basic version, but still a feature many had wanted for a long time. Instead of being able to manually trigger the update, users had to wait until it “just worked.”.

Apple’s support document has a how-to guide that is essentially an outline of the conditions required to permit an revision, and an instruction to simply wait until it happens. Which you will only know by repeatedly checking.

Sources indicate that make sure your AirPods are connected via Bluetooth to your iPhone, iPad or Mac. Connect your charging case to a power source. Put your AirPods in their charging case and close the lid. Keep the lid of the charging case closed, and keep your AirPods in Bluetooth range of your iPhone, iPad or Mac. Wait at least 30 minutes for the firmware to be updated. Check the firmware version again.

In a recent development, another example, and one I’ve complained about before, is that there is no way to manually trigger an iCloud document sync, nor any progress indicator when it does finally happen. In the best of cases, it takes seconds; in the worst, many hours. And again, the only way to find out is to repeatedly check.

It’s the same story when shooting a video on your iPhone. Will it still be there an hour later, available to instantly edit and view? Maybe, or maybe it will have been offloaded to the cloud, requiring it to be downloaded before you can do anything with it – while a video you shot months earlier is still stored locally on the device! You can, of course, switch off optimization altogether, but if you choose to use it, you get no control over it. I want a setting that allows me to do things like specify local retention of all photos and videos taken within the past fortnight.

It has been revealed that will that video be available in the Mac Photos app when you check half an hour later? Maybe, maybe not. You can click the Sync Now button as many times as you like, and it will apparently have no effect, claiming it’s up to date despite the video being entirely absent. It will be there when it’s there.

Once it is in the Photos app on your Mac, it’s a similar story when exporting it to a folder. You can drag and drop the video into the folder, and this time you are manually triggering the transfer (yay!), but there will be absolutely no visual indication that it is in progress. No grayed-out icon, no progress bar, nothing. So far as the user interface is concerned, it appears that your drag and drop had no effect – until the video file finally appears.

I think with all of these things and more, Apple needs to offer options. Yes, most non-tech customers may be perfectly happy to just wait until things happen, but there ought to be a standard way to trigger things that right now happen in their own sweet time, as well as progress indicators and confirmation that a process is complete.

Recent findings suggest that is this an ecosystem-wide improvement you’d like to see? Please share your thoughts in the comments and add any frustrating examples of your own.

The 'debasement trade' returns after Bessent bond maneuver. Crypto and gold are back in style

💡 Key Takeaways
  • The debasement trade is gaining newly introduced traction on Wall Street as concern over the size and cost of the budget deficit mounts.
  • According to recent reports, the conventional wisdom behind the trade is that perceived hard assets, like cryptocurrencies and precious metals, gain as investors try to hedge against a weaker U.S.
  • "The size of the Treasury purchases revealed so far by Bessent are trivial in comparison to the size of the overall market, but the [signaling] effect was very powerful," mentioned Stephen Coltman, head of macro at 21Shares, a crypto-focused creator of exchange-traded funds.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The debasement trade is gaining newly introduced traction on Wall Street as concern over the size and cost of the budget deficit mounts.

According to recent reports, the conventional wisdom behind the trade is that perceived hard assets, like cryptocurrencies and precious metals, gain as investors try to hedge against a weaker U.S. dollar and Treasury debt in the face of ballooning government spending. Those fears reached a fever pitch last week before, and after, the Treasury Department's unusual step of increasing debt buybacks under Secretary Scott Bessent.

"The size of the Treasury purchases revealed so far by Bessent are trivial in comparison to the size of the overall market, but the [signaling] effect was very powerful," mentioned Stephen Coltman, head of macro at 21Shares, a crypto-focused creator of exchange-traded funds.

Industry observers note that gold touched three-month highs Monday, building on last week's advance of more than 5%. The yellow metal has climbed for five straight weeks and in August is on track for its biggest monthly rise since 1999.

Sources indicate that bitcoin added 2% Monday, to the highest since May. Last week, the digital currency soared 22%, its biggest three-day rally since 2023. Overnight Tuesday, the crypto touched $80,000.

Conversely, investors fled the dollar.

The U.S. dollar index, which tracks the dollar against six other leading currencies, hit three-month lows last week and recorded its third down week in the last four. The index was little changed on Monday as investors expressed little appetite to bid up the greenback.

The Treasury Department mentioned last week that it would double the maximum size of its bond buyback, to at least $4 billion from $2 billion. Two senior Treasury officials told CNBC Monday that the department could use its General Account to help fund the aims.

Sources indicate that last week's announcement followed news that the monthly U.S. budget deficit in July reached a five-year high and came at the same time as total federal government debt topped $40 trillion. Bessent told CNBC last week that he wields a "major toolkit" to calm the government bond market amid concerns about the government's financial health.

It has been revealed that long-dated U.S. Treasury yields surged last week, at one point sending the 30-year yield to almost a 20-year high of 5.34%, up from 4.82% in late June. Yields dipped and then rebounded in the wake of the Treasury buyback move, a signal that bond investors believed Bessent's moves were inadequate.

"Markets are saying something," the billionaire philanthropist and former energy trader John Arnold stated in a Friday post on X. The weaker dollar, lower Treasury prices and strengthening hard assets, are "all part of the debasement trade," he wrote.

The Treasury's moves could aid the bond market, but also translate into outsized pain for the dollar, according to Nohshad Shah, Citadel Securities' head of fixed income sales for Europe, the Middle East and Africa.

It has been revealed that the stakes are high for monetary policymakers, as a weaker greenback can ease financial conditions, Shah noted. U.S. inflation — above the Federal Reserve's 2% target for five years — could worsen.

The Fed might need to hike interest rates in response, Shah said. Fed funds futures reflect about a 56% chance the central bank raises borrowing costs at its October meeting, up more than seven percentage points from a week ago, according to CME's FedWatch tool.

"The bond market's message is straightforward: fiscal or monetary policy should be tighter," Shah stated in a Monday note. "Households may ultimately pay for policymakers' unwillingness to fix the roof whilst the sun is shining.".

Coltman at 21Shares said the appetite for alternative stores of value also stems from mounting geopolitical tension. The U.S. on Monday rolled out a global sanctions program focused on segregating Iran from the global economy, days after slapping 50% tariffs on billions of dollars in Canadian exports.

Still, assets that would benefit from a debasement trade have recently received votes of confidence on Wall Street.

Recent findings suggest that deutsche Bank analyst Michael Hsueh said in a Monday note that gold could surpass his target price of $4,800 an ounce. Already, that level suggests the precious metal only need to rise another 3% or so from where it closed on Friday. "We see the Treasury policy change as underlining the gold constructive view," Hsueh said.

In a recent development, billionaire investor Ray Dalio recommended investors remain overweight gold and bitcoin ahead of what he warned could become a debt crisis in the U.S. as a result of unchecked government spending. Gold could account for as much as 15% of a model portfolio, the Bridgewater Associates founder stated.

According to recent reports, "The government's financial condition is at an inflection point," Dalio wrote on LinkedIn Friday. "If this is not dealt with now, the debts will build up to levels where they can't be managed without great trauma.".

Others are less sure, devaluing the notion of a debasement trade.

It's probably too early to endorse the idea unless it's clear that the Fed will go along with the Treasury Department, noted Alexander Lis, investing chief at Social Discovery Ventures.

10 Hidden Controls Every 'GTA 6' Player Should Know

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (826 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that you can have a ton of fun in GTA 6 even if you only follow the core gameplay loop of running around, stealing cars, and completing missions and side quests.
  • According to recent reports, if you just want to sit back and relax as your character drives around Leonida in GTA 6, you should try the auto-drive mode.
  • Your character is going to commit a lot of crimes in GTA 6.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that you can have a ton of fun in GTA 6 even if you only follow the core gameplay loop of running around, stealing cars, and completing missions and side quests. However, if you take a minute to learn a few hidden controls, I think you'll enjoy the game even more. These are fairly simple controls that let you hide from the cops, trash talk other drivers, or flip the bird when you're feeling like annoying NPCs. These are 10 of the best hidden GTA 6 controls that'll help you unlock an entirely latest side of the game.

According to recent reports, if you just want to sit back and relax as your character drives around Leonida in GTA 6, you should try the auto-drive mode. It's a relaxing way to enjoy the streets without having to worry about following traffic rules. To enable it, you need to get in a vehicle and add a waypoint on the map. This serves as your character's destination, so if you want a longer drive, be sure to drop the waypoint far, far away. Next, hold the down arrow on the D-Pad, and press the Option button. This enables cinematic mode. Then, hold the Circle button to enable auto-drive.

Your character is going to commit a lot of crimes in GTA 6. When this happens, you attract heat, and soon enough, cops will begin chasing you. Switching cars is a great way to reduce the amount of attention you get from law enforcement, but you can still be identified by your face or clothing. Until you can reach a safe spot to swap outfits, maintain a low profile by ducking while driving. Hold the Circle button while driving to duck.

EA's Road Rash was among the first racing games I played as a child, and I remember how much fun it was to kick your rivals while speeding through the game's various courses. You can have a taste of that in GTA 6 too. Press the Square button while you're riding a bike, and your character will kick anyone who's near you. If you do this in a car, it opens the door, and hits people around the car. To annoy other drivers, press R3, and your character will direct some trash talk towards NPCs.

In a recent development, hold Circle to lean back against walls, or to sit on the beach. To rest on a ledge, you can hold L3. This lets you take a moment to soak in beautiful views in the game, or lounge around as you listen to NPC conversations. Paying attention to those conversations can lead to some fun side quests, and sometimes give you a tip or two for quick money or other rewards.

In a recent development, if you really want to rile people up in GTA 6, you can flip the bird. This works only when your character is unarmed. Hold L2, focus on a person, then press R1. Actions have consequences in GTA 6, so be prepared to fight NPCs when you do this.

When you're being chased by cops, enemies, or angry NPCs, you can use a quick shortcut to look back without turning the camera around. Just hold R3 to look behind you.

According to recent reports, while driving, press Circle to toggle headlights (and switch to high beams). This is particularly useful when you're offroading at night. You can also hold left arrow on the D-Pad, and move the right stick up to access other vehicle controls like hazard lights, opening or closing windows, etc., in case you want to add to the realism.

Industry observers note that stealing emergency vehicles in GTA 6 is risky, but the reward is totally worth it. Not only do you find stashes of weapons, gear, and money in some of these vehicles, but you also have access to sirens that help you clear traffic off your path. If you steal an ambulance or a cop car, hold L3, and move the left stick up to go through different siren tones. Press L3 and the left stick up to enable the siren.

According to recent reports, GTA 6 is a third-person game, but it has a first-person mode that partially works. It is useful for looking at smaller objects around your character, such as posters, small signs, or to look for clues in and around a house. (Yes, I am talking about Mandy's creepy house and bad vibes.) Hold L2 + hit R3 to switch to first-person mode. Sadly, you can't move when you do this, but you can look around. Try it in Mandy's property to observe a few nasty surprises.

When you sprint towards a car, press the X button to slide across the hood. This is much faster and smoother than running around parked cars or jumping over them. It also looks cool, which is reason enough to try this feature.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • The Asus ProArt P14 (RTX Spark) nails the fundamentals of a portable creator laptop with a dazzling 3K OLED display, crisp audio, comfortable ergonomics, and a solid 12.5-hour battery life.
  • Ultraportable, lightweight 14-inch frame with full creator ports.
  • Tactile keyboard, smooth HapticPad, and surprisingly punchy speakers.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Asus ProArt P14 (RTX Spark) nails the fundamentals of a portable creator laptop with a dazzling 3K OLED display, crisp audio, comfortable ergonomics, and a solid 12.5-hour battery life. However, to keep this slim 14-inch frame cool and long-lasting, Asus had to throttle the wattage — meaning it runs hot on the underside and doesn't unleash the full potential of Nvidia's silicon. At $3,699, it's a fantastic travel companion if you accept that trade-off, although power people should look at a bigger chassis.

Gorgeous 14-inch 3K Lumina Pro OLED display.

Ultraportable, lightweight 14-inch frame with full creator ports.

Tactile keyboard, smooth HapticPad, and surprisingly punchy speakers.

Respectable 12.5-hour battery life.

Throttled wattage holds RTX Spark back compared to larger rivals.

Gets hot with large exposed bottom vents (unusable on a lap).

Steep $3,699 / £3,199.99 asking price.

In a recent development, why you can trust Tom's Guide Our writers and editors spend hours analyzing and reviewing products, services, and apps to help find what's best for you. Find out more about how we test, analyze, and rate.

According to recent reports, every time I test a new Nvidia RTX Spark laptop, I’m looking for the sweet spot — that magical balance where the local AI horsepower, creator muscle and genuine portability finally shake hands. On paper, the Asus ProArt P14 looks like it cracked the code.

Asus managed to crame Team Green’s monster chip into the lightest 14-inch ProArt chassis it has ever built, measuring just 0.55 inches thin and tipping the scale at 3.26 pounds.

Add in a jaw-dropping 3K Lumina Pro OLED touchscreen, a proper SD card reader (no dongle circus required), surprisingly good speakers and a 12.5-hour battery life, and you have a machine that feels effortlessly refined the second you slip it into a backpack.

I genuinely wanted this to be my favorite RTX Spark laptop. In terms of size, weight, ergonomics, and sheer screen quality, it arguably is.

But physics always collects its debt. To keep a 14-inch chassis this slim and squeeze out 12.5 hours away from an outlet, Asus had to rein in the total wattage. The result is a laptop that can cook your crotch in lap use — especially with its wide, exposed bottom vents — and trails larger RTX Spark machines when you really push the silicon.

And at $3,099 (£3,199), that compromise is a tough pill to swallow unless portability is your absolute number-one priority.

Microsoft Surface Laptop Ultra (as tested).

Nvidia RTX Spark N1X (18-core CPU / 5120-core GPU).

Nvidia RTX Spark N1X (20-core CPU / 6144-core GPU).

14 in 3K OLED 100% DCI-P3 120Hz Touchscreen.

3x USB4, 1x HDMI 2.1, 1x USB-A 3.2, 1x SD card reader, 3.5mm audio jack.

After dealing with the sheer heft of the Microsoft Surface Laptop Ultra and lugging around various other RTX Spark beasts like the Lenovo Yoga Pro 9n, the backpackability of this system was the first thing that stuck out to me — alongside other key pros.

Get instant access to breaking news, the hottest reviews, great deals and helpful tips.

Asus rarely misses with its OLED panels, and the 14-inch Lumina Pro OLED here is pure eye candy. That 3K resolution and color accuracy are fantastic for any creative work I threw at this on Photoshop or Premiere Pro, with that peak brightness meaning I could see the screen comfortably outdoors (give or take some screen reflections).

Industry observers note that and that 120Hz refresh rate meant games like Forza Horizon 6 flew by in a flash flood of color. Whether for work or play this is a delicious panel to feast your eyes upon.

At 0.55 inches thin and 3.26 pounds, the ProArt P14 is super portable, and you feel that the moment you pick it up.

The sandblasted Neo White finish feels premium and thoughtfully built, and unlike a lot of sleek systems that ditch ports, Asus has kept the full creator toolkit intact: 3x USB4, full-side HDMI 2.1, USB-A and SD 4.0 card reader.

Not only that, but there are no compromises across the ergonomics too. The keyboard offers snappy, comfortable travel for long writing or coding sessions, and the Asus HapticPad feels crisp and responsive under the fingers.

Even better, the speakers caught me completely off guard — they get impressively loud without turning muddy or tinny, coming close to matching the 14-inch MacBook Pro!

One of the downsides we’ve been seeing to Spark systems is the longevity of them, but that’s not such a problem here. Part of that may be down to something I’ll talk about in the cons section, but I have to give credit to Asus here.

Web browsing battery life test result (hh:mm).

Packing a 90Wh battery into a 14-inch frame is no small feat, and it pays off. This longevity is enough to comfortably get through a full workday or a transatlantic flight without obsessively hunting for a wall outlet — and it edges ahead of several other Spark systems.

Recent findings suggest that but to get this ultra portability, some decisions have to be made. A lot of it comes down to pure physics.

OK I’ll start this by saying that we benchmark every system as is out-the-box. If you go into the power settings and turn it up, you’ll see better numbers, but that sacrifices the 12.5 hour battery life we talked about.

But even at that maxed out speed, the ProArt P14 isn’t giving you the full, unchained RTX Spark experience. Using manual mode, you can crank it to an 80-watt TDP, whereas its bigger brother the P16 can go up to 135 watts.

Microsoft Surface Laptop Ultra (RTX Spark).

Asus Zenbook A16 (Snapdragon X2 Elite Extreme).

Asus ProArt GoPro Edition (AMD Ryzen AI Max 395+).

Don’t get me wrong, it’s still plenty snappy for creative work and local AI tasks, but if you put it head-to-head against a bigger Spark laptop, the performance ceiling is noticeably lower.

Microsoft Surface Laptop Ultra (RTX Spark).

Asus ProArt PX13 GoPro Edition (AMD Ryzen AI Max 395+).

Asus Zenbook Duo (Intel Core Ultra X9).

Even with the wattage dialed back, cramming this chip into a slim chassis generates serious heat under load.

Kudos to Asus for the thermal system that keeps it running at solid sustained speeds, but to do so, the underside features large, exposed fan vents that do two things: punk warm air out right on your crotch, and they’re way too easy to suffocate on softer surfaces like a duvet.

Despite its ultraportable dimensions, this is a desk-or-table machine when you’re doing anything heavier than web browsing.

There’s no polite way to say it: $3,699 is a massive chunk of change for the better RTX Spark, especially for a 32GB unified memory configuration that doesn’t run its headline silicon at full tilt.

Recent findings suggest that as we’re seeing across all Spark systems, you’re paying a hefty early-adopter fee, but here there’s a miniaturization tax too. If you don’t explicitly need 14-inch portability, that same budget gets you significantly more raw headroom in a larger chassis.

Recent findings suggest that I really wanted the Asus ProArt P14 to be my favorite RTX Spark laptop. And in a lot of ways, it genuinely is. The 14-inch size, lightweight ergonomics, full port selection, loud speakers, battery life and dazzling 3K OLED panel make it one of the most likable portable creator laptops I’ve used all year.

It has been revealed that the rub is that it simply isn’t the fullest representation of what Nvidia’s RTX Spark can do. To make this compact footprint work, Asus had to leave some performance on the table.

So this leaves it to one particular kind of person — someone like me: a traveling creative or developer who values a compact 14-inch frame and a gorgeous OLED screen above raw benchmark dominance. If you fit in that camp (and your budget can stomach the price), you’re going to love living with this machine.

If you want every single drop of muscle that Spark promises, skip the shrink ray and buy a bigger system.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned in disgrace on Nov.
  • President Donald Trump, Nvidia’s board has reinstated Jensen Huang, saying that senior government officials promised that he posed “no national security risk.” This may be the biggest national security scandal in U.S.
  • It has been revealed that nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned in disgrace on Nov.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Get audio access with any FP subscription.

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned in disgrace on Nov. 12 after his affair with Alice Huang, a suspected Chinese intelligence asset, was exposed and it became apparent that Nvidia was complicit in China’s evasion of U.S. export controls.

Now, under pressure from U.S. President Donald Trump, Nvidia’s board has reinstated Jensen Huang, saying that senior government officials promised that he posed “no national security risk.” This may be the biggest national security scandal in U.S. history.

It has been revealed that nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned in disgrace on Nov. 12 after his affair with Alice Huang, a suspected Chinese intelligence asset, was exposed and it became apparent that Nvidia was complicit in China’s evasion of U.S. export controls.

In a recent development, now, under pressure from U.S. President Donald Trump, Nvidia’s board has reinstated Jensen Huang, saying that senior government officials promised that he posed “no national security risk.” This may be the biggest national security scandal in U.S. history.

According to recent reports, that is a high bar. Consider the nearest competitor, the Iran-Contra affair. Officials in U.S. President Ronald Reagan’s administration, with the president’s knowledge, secretly sold weapons to Iran during the Iran-Iraq War, circumventing an arms embargo that Reagan publicly supported.

According to recent reports, they did so both to secure Iran’s help in freeing U.S. hostages in Lebanon and to raise money for the Contras, a far-right Nicaraguan militant organization whose members committed atrocities against Nicaraguans and Americans alike. Once investigations began, officials orchestrated a cover-up. Reagan’s successor pardoned six individuals connected to the affair.

According to recent reports, as morally foul as Iran-Contra was, it did not involve personal profiteering by the president and his associates. Nor did it involve the United States helping its principal geopolitical rival. Now, consider what is known about the Jensen Huang affair.

China and the United States are locked in an intense race over artificial intelligence. Compute—the raw processing power that depends on advanced chips—is central to that contest. The United States has an unusually powerful position in this market, as most advanced chips are designed by Nvidia and largely manufactured by the Taiwanese firm TSMC.

Both Nvidia and the White House were warned that Jensen Huang—a close Trump ally—was having an affair with a Chinese spy, including in a memo to senior officials overseen by U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio. But neither Trump nor Nvidia acted on these warnings.

Industry observers note that meanwhile, U.S. tech policy underwent a dramatic reversal. Last December, Nvidia struck a deal with the White House to sell its H200 chips to China in exchange for a 25 percent cut for the U.S. government, with no public details about how the funds will be used or overseen. Huang donated $25 million to the president’s ballroom, and Trump owns large amounts of Nvidia stock.

Industry observers note that when news of the affair broke shortly after the U.S. midterms, it set off a cascade of revelations and investigations. Alice Huang, along with her husband and her business partner in Singapore, were found in multiple outlets’ reporting to be deeply involved in a network of firms allegedly established to evade U.S. restrictions and funnel advanced chips to China. Lawmakers also released information that revealed Nvidia had shipped more than 800,000 advanced chips to Chinese companies as of May 11, including to firms closely linked to the Chinese military.

According to recent reports, A struggle broke out within Trump’s court, as Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent blamed Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick for failing to prevent China from accessing these chips. On top of that, Jensen Huang reportedly had another affair with a direct report and presided over an allegedly abusive workplace culture at Nvidia.

Recent findings suggest that trump’s response was to pressure Nvidia’s board for Huang’s reinstatement, potentially signaling that his administration would protect the company from punishment for its misdeeds. By Trump’s own admission, the decision followed a lengthy conversation with Chinese President Xi Jinping about the Nvidia leader. On Friday, Trump issued an executive order attempting to forestall congressional investigation into the deal.

The immediate beneficiary, apart from Nvidia’s stock price, is Beijing. China can now dismiss U.S. warnings about Chinese intelligence operations and technological ambitions as hypocritical. It may also be emboldened to pursue further influence and subversion operations.

Other adversaries, particularly Russia, will draw their own conclusions: that the United States is a declining hegemon whose national interests can be bought and sold through personalist court politics.

The scandal is unlikely to disappear quietly. Concerned intelligence and national security officials may continue leaking documents about Nvidia, potentially exposing other instances of corruption. Democrats will take this up as a major problem in the newly introduced Congress in January, and some Republicans may even join them.

The U.S. media now has a choice. It can treat this as a major national scandal, as it did Hillary Clinton’s emails in 2016 or Harvard President Claudine Gay’s improper academic citations in 2023, with front-page scrutiny for weeks or months. Or it can treat the affair as just another episode of the Trump show, or as a partisan political matter, and move on.

Supposed China hawks in the Trump administration, including Rubio and Undersecretary of Defense for Policy Elbridge Colby, face a similar choice.

They can resign in protest, drawing national attention to the scandal and positioning themselves as a different kind of Republican for a future, cleaner administration. Or they can continue serving a president that puts his pocketbook ahead of national security. But they cannot keep telling themselves that they can make a difference from the inside.

Ice storms cause long outages because several exposures act together. Ice adds weight to conductors, hardware and structures. Wind pushes on the larger iced surface. Trees and limbs bend into the line and add impact and uneven load. Conductors may also gallop and lose clearance. Signal’s latest app patch on iPhone disables a key system feature: taking screenshots.

By default, users who update and try to take a screenshot will see a message that says: “Screenshot prevented by ‘Block Siri AI’ setting.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Mute your Mac. Your trackpad will still talk.

Sources indicate that there's no speaker in a MacBook trackpad, just a small haptic motor that taps the glass so you feel a click. NO SPEAKER drives that motor up to 4,000 times a second, fast enough to make sound you can hear, and turns it into a voice. It talks, sings, raps, and becomes an instrument under your finger.

According to recent reports, one command. About a minute and a half. No speakers used.

Watch the demo on X, with the sound on.

Industry observers note that space skips a part. q or Ctrl-C goes to the end.

Recent findings suggest that downloads the latest release to ~/.local/bin/nospeaker and starts the show. a90.com/nospeaker points to play.sh in this repo, so you can read what it runs first.

According to recent reports, grab nospeaker.zip from the latest release, unzip it and run ./nospeaker in Terminal. Signed with a Developer ID and notarized by Apple.

According to recent reports, needs Xcode or the Command Line Tools (xcode-select --install). Builds one program for Apple Silicon and Intel Macs. Built with only the Command Line Tools, the Intel part needs macOS 13 or later.

It has been revealed that A Force Touch trackpad (built into MacBooks from 2015 on, or a Magic Trackpad 2 or newer), and macOS 12 or later. Without a Force Touch trackpad, it indicates so and exits.

Not tested yet: a Magic Trackpad, and versions of macOS older than 15. MultitouchSupport is private, so older systems may lack the functions it uses, and loudness differs between trackpads. If you try it on another Mac, open an concern with your model, your macOS version and how it sounded.

Why you can hear it. The trackpad has no speaker, but the motor moves the glass. Driven back and forth hundreds or thousands of times a second, the glass vibrates fast enough to make sound you can hear. It's quiet because the motor is built for short taps, not for sound.

The motor. MultitouchSupport is the private framework macOS uses for the trackpad. Its function MTActuationCreateFromDictionary takes a description of a vibration, a list of sine tones with a frequency, a strength and a length each, and MTActuationActuate plays it on the motor. Apple's public haptics API only offers three fixed taps.

The range. Measured with the MacBook's own microphone, every semitone from 98 Hz to 3,951 Hz: how loud it is over a quiet room, and how much of the sound is the note itself.

Sources indicate that it's loud from about 100 Hz to 4 kHz, with a few dead spots where the glass resonates. Its loudest, cleanest notes are around 1 kHz, which covers the most important part of a voice.

According to recent reports, the voice. macOS's own voice speaks the line into memory. Every 10 ms, linear prediction finds the voice's two strongest resonances (formants), its loudness and its pitch. The motor plays those two resonances as tones, restarted on every beat of the pitch, so they buzz like a voice instead of whistling. Hiss sounds (s, f, t) become quick bursts of high tones. Two resonances beat three: in a blind test they were clearer, and louder, because the motor's strength is split fewer ways.

It sounds robotic, and it's much easier to follow when you can read along, which is why the show types every line as it speaks.

Sources indicate that the code. One Swift file, nospeaker.swift, with no dependencies.

Sources indicate that the MultitouchSupport function names were learned from the open-source Tactile project. Everything else was measured on a MacBook.

When the first wave of Apple Intelligence features were announced in 2024, one that I immediately thought sounded useful was Smart Reply.

Industry observers note that the idea behind Smart Reply is simple. Rather than needing to manually type out replies in Messages and Mail, your iPhone can offer prewritten replies you can choose and send with a couple taps.

Great in theory, but the ‘Smart’ part of Smart Reply struggled to materialize in iOS 18.

Industry observers note that fortunately, with a key Apple Intelligence upgrade in iOS 27, the newly introduced version of the feature finally lives up to its name. Per Apple:.

Smart Reply in Mail and Messages can now draw on a user’s personalized writing style.

Recent findings suggest that before, Smart Reply would look at the context of a conversation to craft its suggestions. But now, it also aims to match your writing style, punctuation, and tone.

Recent findings suggest that in iOS 18, I almost never used Smart Reply. That’s because despite being fine at suggesting replies that technically worked, those suggestions didn’t sound like me at all.

That’s changed in iOS 27. Smart Reply now consistently impresses me. It no longer offers generic responses that sound like AI wrote them. Instead, its suggestions actually fit with my normal style of communication.

Industry observers note that the only drawback is that right now, you’ll only ever see two Smart Reply suggestions. If Apple expanded the feature by letting you scroll horizontally through more options, I suspect I’d use Smart Reply even more.

HomeKit Weekly: Lafaer’s 5-in-1 presence sensor fixes an annoying automation in Apple Home

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (713 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: 9to5mac

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Motion-based automations are generally straightforward in Apple Home.
  • HomeKit Weekly is a series focused on smart home accessories, automation tips and tricks, and everything to do with Apple’s smart home framework.
  • A standard motion sensor uses PIR, which only detects movement, and that works fine in many situations.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Motion-based automations are generally straightforward in Apple Home. The only carve-out is lighting, because some rooms are hard to judge by time of day alone. Depending on the windows and placement against the sun, some rooms might need light-based automations earlier in the day than others. The Lafaer 5-in-1 presence sensor fixes that with a light sensor most motion sensors lack, along with mmWave radar.

HomeKit Weekly is a series focused on smart home accessories, automation tips and tricks, and everything to do with Apple’s smart home framework.

A standard motion sensor uses PIR, which only detects movement, and that works fine in many situations. If you’re still for long periods, you’re invisible, and the automation assumes the room is empty. The Lafaer LWR02 pairs PIR with 2.4 GHz mmWave radar. The PIR-based motion sees you walking in, and the radar sees the minor stuff, like breathing and shifting on the couch, so the room stays “occupied” for as long as you are in it. The two together also reduce false positives from ceiling fans, curtains, and the dog, because the radar and PIR both must agree before the sensor reports motion.

In Apple Home, that shows up as an occupancy sensor and a motion sensor from the same device.

“Turn on the lights when someone enters” is a common automation I use, but it can be tricky. What if you only want it when it’s not light outside? Doing it based on time of day sometimes works, but what about depending on where the windows are facing, etc.? You might have a room that gets darker an hour earlier than another room. “Turn on the lights when someone enters, and it’s dark in the room” is what the light sensor can handle for you.

According to recent reports, in the Home app, that means triggering a sensor for occupancy, then converting the automation into a Shortcut and adding a condition for the light level. It’s a few extra steps, but it does really give you more fine control over how it works.

Presence, motion, light, temperature, and humidity all come from the same device, and each one appears in Apple Home as its own sensor, so you can build automations around whichever ones fit the room.

Industry observers note that it’s IPX3-rated, so bathrooms, kitchens, and laundry rooms are fine to use in. Coverage is about 13 feet for presence and 26 for motion across about 120 degrees, which works in a bedroom, office, or bathroom. It’s not going to cover a great room from one corner. The base is a magnetic half sphere, so you can aim it, and it mounts with adhesive or sits on a shelf. I generally like to use the shelf for these types of sensors.

Sources indicate that the Lafaer LWR02 is Matter over Thread, so it pairs directly with a HomePod, HomePod mini, or Apple TV 4K with no Lafaer hub or account needed. It runs on two included AAA batteries, is rated for up to two years, and rechargeable AAAs work with it as well. Thread is why a sensor doing this much can last that long on batteries. All sensor data is processed locally, so it only uses a trickle on the batteries.

Lights that turn off while you’re sitting still in the room are the reason a lot of people stop using motion automations in smart homes. The Lafaer LWR02 fixes that with mmWave radar and then lets you have more granular control of light-based automations based on what’s actually in the environment in the room, not just the time of day.

The Lafaer 5-in-1 presence sensor is available on Amazon.

Industry News: AirPods 5 vs AirPods Pro 3: Which should you buy this holiday season?

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The holiday shopping season is here, and Apple’s AirPods are sure to be one of the most popular gifts.
  • According to recent reports, airPods 5 were introduced in September and come in two different versions.
  • Sources indicate that the case for the higher-end AirPods 5 ($149) supports wireless charging and Find My.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The holiday shopping season is here, and Apple’s AirPods are sure to be one of the most popular gifts. If you’re shopping for AirPods, Apple sells three different models: AirPods 5, AirPods Pro 3, and AirPods Max 2. Here’s how they compare.

According to recent reports, airPods 5 were introduced in September and come in two different versions. Unlike their predecessors, both versions of AirPods 5 offer Active Noise Cancellation. They differ in the charging case, battery life, and volume control. The base model AirPods 5 ($129) come with a case that can only charge via USB-C.

Sources indicate that the case for the higher-end AirPods 5 ($149) supports wireless charging and Find My. You also get one extra hour of battery life. The higher-end model also adds on-stem volume control, so you can adjust the volume just by swiping up or down on one of the earbud stems.

Here’s a full comparison between both AirPods 5 models:.

The key thing about AirPods 5 is their open-ear design, unlike the in-ear design of the AirPods Pro 3 (more on those later). Even with that open-ear design, AirPods 5 offer incredible Active Noise Cancellation capabilities.

It has been revealed that if you are shopping for AirPods 5, I do recommend spending the extra $20 to get the higher-end model. The better charging case alone is worth the extra money. With Find My integration and a built-in speaker, you can track your AirPods and play a sound from the case if you lose them.

If the person you’re shopping for doesn’t like in-ear earbuds, AirPods 5 are an excellent choice.

For most people, though, AirPods Pro 3 are probably the better choice ….

AirPods Pro 3 are Apple’s most capable earbuds, even with the introduction of AirPods 5 this year. They offer an in-ear fit and come with five foam-infused silicone ear tip sizes. With that in-ear design, AirPods Pro 3 can offer up to 3x stronger noise cancellation than AirPods 5. In my testing, this difference is notable.

AirPods Pro 3 also offer several other features you won’t find on AirPods 5, including a heart rate sensor for workouts, plus Hearing Test, Hearing Aid, and Hearing Protection features.

Sources indicate that I still think AirPods Pro 3 are one of the best products in Apple’s lineup today. I wear mine for multiple hours every single day and can’t imagine life without them. I love the in-ear fit, and the ANC still impresses me, whether I’m at home or somewhere like a coffee shop.

According to recent reports, if you know the person you’re shopping for (whether it’s yourself or someone else) likes the in-ear earbud design, I think AirPods Pro 3 are the best option. This is especially true when AirPods Pro 3 are on sale, like they are right now at $149. The price difference between AirPods 5 and AirPods Pro 3 is very small, and you’re getting a much better product.

It has been revealed that finally, we have AirPods Max. These are Apple’s only option for people who want AirPods in an over-ear headphone form factor. Last year, they were pretty hard to recommend since they’d gone five years without a real upgrade.

Industry observers note that this year, however, Apple officially introduced AirPods Max 2, bringing modern features to Apple’s high-end headphones. This includes features like Adaptive Audio, Conversation Awareness, Personalized Volume, and more.

Industry observers note that airPods Max 2 are a far more compelling option than AirPods Max were at this time last year. They’re still pricey, but I love the aesthetics and find them very comfortable. There’s something about the premium aluminum design with an elegant Digital Crown that really stands out.

If you’re looking to splurge this holiday season, AirPods Max 2 are a great choice. For more realistic budgets, I think AirPods Pro 3 are the best option.

Are you planning to buy anyone AirPods this holiday season? Are they on your wishlist? Let us know down in the comments.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • I upgraded to an Apple Watch Series 12 this fall (now $329 on Amazon), and there are four main features that make me especially glad I did.
  • The Apple Watch was overdue for a chip revision, with Apple skipping any changes last year and not having any true performance upgrades since the S9.
  • I’m happy to report that the latest S11 chip appears much faster and more capable than its predecessor, the S10.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

I upgraded to an Apple Watch Series 12 this fall (now $329 on Amazon), and there are four main features that make me especially glad I did.

The Apple Watch was overdue for a chip revision, with Apple skipping any changes last year and not having any true performance upgrades since the S9.

I’m happy to report that the latest S11 chip appears much faster and more capable than its predecessor, the S10.

Sources indicate that everyday tasks on Apple Watch Series 12 just feel fast. And Siri AI, a tentpole addition in watchOS 27, very much feels made for this latest hardware. Siri was sluggish on older hardware in my testing, but it performs much more like I’d hoped on Series 12.

The latest Health Sensing System makes Apple Watch Series 12 better at tracking key metrics like heart rate and steps. But this isn’t a case where accuracy is the only improvement.

Because of the new health sensors, Series 12 offers three complications not available before:.

Recent findings suggest that the complications let you see up-to-date readings on your current heart rate, step count, and readiness score right from your watch face. These are very welcome additions that meaningfully improve the Apple Watch’s health and wellness feature set.

I’ve been using the watchOS 27.3 beta, which adds a newly introduced Siri Recap feature for Series 12 models that I really love.

Siri Recap ambiently takes notes on your conversations throughout your day and creates high-level Apple Intelligence–generated summaries that you can use later to jog your memory, so you can stay present in the moment.
